recipes.name: Acciughe alla Marinara (Anchovies in the Sailor's Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Prepare anchovies in an oil-based stew with minced garlic, parsley, salt, pepper and oil.
When almost cooked, add a little water mixed with vinegar.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Acciughe Fritte (Fried Anchovies)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the head from the anchovies and coat them with flour.
Take them one by one by the tail, dip them in beaten and well-salted egg.
Dip them again in flour and fry them in a pan with boiling oil.
For a better result with larger fish, open them along the back by cutting with a fine knife and remove the spine, leaving them joined at the tail.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Acetosa di Lampone (Raspberry Vinegar)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Form this vinegar by substituting excellent quality wine vinegar for citric acid, which is poured into the raspberry syrup when it is removed from the fire
Regulate the dose of vinegar by tasting, putting in a little at first and tasting the syrup in a little water, increasing the dose as needed
This beverage will be more refreshing than the others and equally pleasant

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Agnello all'Orientale (Oriental-Style Lamb)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Lard the lamb entirely with a larding needle using strips of lard seasoned with salt and pepper.
Oil it with butter and milk or with milk alone and salt it halfway through cooking.
Roast it on a spit until tender and delicate.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Agnello coi Piselli all'Uso di Romagna (Lamb with Peas Romagna Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: a quarter of lamb from the hind part
two cloves of garlic cut into strips
a piece of lard or a slice of cured meat
tomato juice or tomato preserve dissolved in broth or water

steps: Take a quarter of lamb from the hind part, lard it with two cloves of garlic cut into strips and with some sprigs of rosemary.
Take a piece of lard or a slice of cured meat and mince them finely with a knife.
Put the lamb on the fire in a pan with this battuto and a little oil; season with salt and pepper and let it brown.
When it has taken color, add a small piece of butter, tomato juice or tomato preserve dissolved in broth or water, and cook it until perfectly done.
Remove the lamb for a moment, pour the peas into the sauce, and when they have boiled a little, put it back on them, cook them together, and serve them as a side dish.
The same method can be used to cook a piece of milk veal in the loin or rump.
In Tuscany these dishes are prepared in the same manner, but only oil is used.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Agnello in Frittata (Lamb in Omelet)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cut a lamb loin, which is the part that best lends itself to this dish, into small pieces and fry it in pure lard; little is enough because in that place the meat is rather fatty.
At mid-cooking season the lamb with salt and pepper and when it is totally cooked pour in four or five beaten eggs and lightly seasoned also with salt and pepper.
Mix, making sure the eggs set only slightly.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Agnello in Umido (Braised Lamb)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Two young onions or three to four small white onions

steps: Slice the onions and sauté them in a piece of butter until they take on a deep red color
Add the lamb and season with salt and pepper
Wait for the meat to begin to color and add another piece of butter dusted with flour; stir and let it take on a nice color
Finish cooking the meat with broth added little by little
Serve not dry, but with a certain amount of its gravy

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Agnello Trippato (Lamb with Egg Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 500 grams of lamb from the loin

steps: Cut 500 grams of lamb from the loin into small pieces and fry it with virgin lard.

Make a soffritto in a pan with the fat remaining in the pan, garlic, and parsley, and when the garlic has taken color, throw in the already fried lamb, season with salt and pepper, turn it well, and leave it on the fire for a while so the seasoning incorporates.
Then bind it with the following sauce: beat in a pot two eggs with a good pinch of grated parmesan and half a lemon.
Pour it into the lamb, stir, and when the egg has somewhat set, serve at table.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Albicocche in Composta (Apricots in Compote)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make an incision in the apricots to remove the pit in such a way that they do not spoil, and place them on the fire with the aforementioned water
When this begins to boil, pour in the sugar and, shaking the saucepan from time to time, let them cook

Once they become soft and somewhat wrinkled, remove them one by one with a spoon and place them in a compote dish; drain the liquid they have brought from the saucepan and let the remaining water reduce on the fire, which you will pour into the compote dish over the apricots when it has thickened like a syrup
Serve them cold

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Amaretti I (Almond Macaroons)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Peel the almonds and dry them in the sun or by the fire, then chop them very fine with a crescent-shaped chopper.

Work the sugar and the whites with a spoon for at least half an hour, and add the almonds to form a stiff paste so as to make little balls the size of a small walnut; if it turns out too soft add more sugar and if too hard another bit of white, this time beaten.
If you would like to give the macaroons a color tending toward brown, mix a little burnt sugar into the mixture.
As you form the said balls, which you will flatten to the thickness of a centimeter, place them on wafers or on pieces of paper.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Amaretti I (Bitter Almond Macaroons)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Blanch the almonds and dry them in the sun or by fire, then chop them very finely with a crescent-shaped knife.

Work the sugar and egg whites together with a wooden spoon for at least half an hour, and add the almonds to form a firm paste from which to make small balls about the size of a small walnut; if it turns out too soft add more sugar and if too hard add a little more egg white, this time whipped.
If you wish to give the macaroons a color tending toward brown, mix a little browned sugar into the mixture.

As you form the said balls, flatten them to the thickness of one centimeter, place them on wafers or on pieces of paper, or in a baking pan buttered and sprinkled with half flour and half powdered sugar; but at a reasonable distance from one another because they spread a lot and puff up, remaining hollow inside.
Bake them in an oven at moderate heat.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Amaretti II (Bitter Almond Macaroons, Second Recipe)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Blanch the almonds and dry them in the sun or by fire; then pound them fine in a mortar with one egg white poured in several times.
Having done this, mix in half the sugar, working the mixture with a hand.
After pour it into a bowl and, always working so it incorporates, add half an egg white, then the other half of the sugar and afterwards the last half egg white.
You will obtain, thus worked, a homogeneous mixture of proper consistency that you can shape into a stick to cut into equal pieces.
Pick them up one by one with slightly dampened hands to form balls about the size of walnuts.

Flatten them to the thickness of one centimeter and for the rest proceed as for the previous ones, but sprinkle them lightly with powdered sugar before putting them in a hot oven, and I say oven because a country oven would not be suitable for this paste.
With this amount you will obtain about thirty macaroons.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anatra Domestica (Braised Domestic Duck)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Prepare it like the mallard duck (recipe 270) and put it on the fire with a similar mixture of finely chopped vegetables.
When the duck has taken color, bathe it with tomato sauce or tomato paste and bring it to cook with water or broth.
Strain the sauce, remove the excess fat and put it back on the fire with the duck and a small piece of butter.
With this sauce and Parmigiano cheese you can dress a soup of strips or homemade lasagne noodles and serve the duck with a side of vegetables cooked in a little of that same sauce.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anatra Domestica Arrosto (Roasted Domestic Duck)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lard, in wide and thin slices

steps: Salt it inside and wrap the entire breast with wide and thin slices of lard held in place with string.
Brush it with oil and salt it when cooking is almost complete.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anatra Domestica col Contorno di Riso (Domestic Duck with Rice Garnish)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a mixture with a quarter of a large onion and all the herbs, that is parsley, carrot and celery chopped together with 50 grams of fat and lean prosciutto.
Put it on the fire with two tablespoons of oil and the duck on top, seasoned with salt and pepper.

Once browned, bathe it with tomato sauce or tomato paste and the necessary water to bring it to cook, adding at the same time a pinch of dried mushrooms to cook in that sauce which will then be strained through a sieve and defatted, keeping the mushrooms to add to the rice.

Put the rice, in the amount of 200 grams, raw as is, in a pot with 40 grams of butter and when it begins to take color pour hot water little by little, giving it flavor with the duck sauce and Parmigiano cheese when you are about to remove it from the fire.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anguilla Arrosto (Roasted Eel)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: If the eel is large and you want to cook it on a spit, it is better to skin it.
Cut it into pieces three centimeters long and thread them between two croutons with some sage or laurel leaves if you don't fear that the latter, for its too sharp smell, will turn your stomach.
Cook it plain over moderate heat and finally give it a good flame to make a crispy crust.
For seasoning, salt only and lemon wedges when brought to the table.
Alternatively, for medium-sized eel, roast it on a grill with its skin, which when softened with lemon juice at the table can offer a pleasant flavor when sucked.
Season with salt and pepper only. The eels require red and dry wine to accompany them.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anguilla coi piselli (Eel with Peas)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Stew it as in the recipe for Stewed Eel, and when it is cooked remove it dry to cook the peas in its sauce.
Put it back among the peas to reheat it and serve it.
No tomato juice is used here, but water if needed.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anguilla col vino (Eel with Wine)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: One eel of about half a kilogram or more than one of the same total weight

steps: Rub the eels with sand to clean them of mucus, wash them, and cut them into chunks.
Place in a pan one garlic clove cut into thin slices, three or four sage leaves cut roughly, the rind of a quarter lemon, and not much oil.
Put it on the fire, and when the soffritto has taken on color, place the eels in it and season with salt and pepper.
When the stew begins to reduce, loosen them with the tip of a knife so they do not stick, and brown them on one side.
Brown them on the other side, pour in a good finger of red or white dry wine mixed with two fingers of water, cover them, and let them finish cooking over low heat.
Serve them at table with some of their sauce and serve to four people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anguilla in Gratella (Grilled Eel)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Place the medium eel on a grill with its skin.
Season with salt and pepper only at half cooking.
The lemon juice softens the skin when it is brought to the table and can offer a pleasant flavor when sucked.
Eat them hot.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anguilla in umido (Stewed Eel)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: If the eels are large, do not peel them; cut them into short pieces.
Finely chop a generous amount of onion and parsley, put it on the fire with a little oil, pepper, and salt.
When the onion has taken on color, add the eel.
Wait for it to absorb the flavor of the soffritto, then finish cooking it with tomato juice or tomato preserve dissolved in water.
Ensure there remains plenty of sauce if you want to serve it at table over barely toasted bread slices.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anguilla in umido all'uso di Comacchio (Stewed Eel Comacchio Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cut all the vegetables except the lemon into large pieces and boil them with water, salt, and pepper.
Cut the eels into chunks, leaving the chunks connected to each other by a strip of flesh.

Take a suitable pot and make a layer of eel at the bottom, then layer the vegetables mentioned above that are almost cooked (discarding the lemon), then another layer of eel, another of vegetables, and so on until everything is used.
Cover everything with the water in which the vegetables boiled.
Put the well-sealed pot to boil slowly, shaking and turning it, but never stirring with a spoon as you would break everything up.
Surround the pot with ash and embers up to more than halfway, in front of a clear wood fire, always shaking and turning.
When the chunks, which were connected by a strip, become detached from each other, they are almost cooked.
Add a good spoonful of strong vinegar and tomato preserve, taste the broth to correct the salt and pepper (be generous), give it a few more boils, and serve the pot at table.
Serve in hot dishes on bread slices.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anguille alla fiorentina (Eels Florentine Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Clean the eels by making a circular incision under the head, holding it firmly with a cloth to prevent slipping due to the fish's abundant mucus, and pull down the skin which will come off entirely.
Cut the eels into pieces about one finger length or slightly less, and season them with oil, salt, and pepper, leaving them to rest for one or two hours.
Use an iron pan or earthenware dish, cover the bottom with a thin layer of oil, two whole garlic cloves, and sage leaves.
Sauté briefly, then take the eel pieces one at a time, coat them in breadcrumbs, and arrange them in the pan side by side, pouring the remaining seasoning over them.
Cook them between two fires, and when they have taken on color, pour a little water into the pan.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Animelle alla Bottiglia (Sweetbreads in Bottle Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lamb sweetbreads or from larger animals
Optional: meat broth, butter and flour for sauce

steps: Those of lamb need no preparation; those of larger animals must be given half-cooking in water, skinning them if necessary. Leave the first ones whole, cut the second ones into pieces and flour all of them well and put them to brown in butter seasoning them with salt and pepper. Then moisten them with Marsala or Madeira wine, and after make them come to a single boil. You can also make the sauce separately with a pinch of flour, a small piece of butter and the wine.
If you enhance them with meat sauce, from being good as they are, they will become exquisite.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Anolini alla Parmigiana (Parmesan-Style Anolini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lean beef from the thigh, boneless, 500 grams
One quarter of a medium onion
Breadcrumbs from day-old bread, lightly toasted, 100 grams
One egg and the meat broth
Three eggs for the pasta sheets

steps: Lard the piece of meat, tie it and season with salt, pepper and spice scent, then put it on the fire in an earthenware pot or casserole with butter and finely chopped onion to brown it with the butter.
Pour two ladle-fuls of broth into the pot and close it with several sheets of paper held secure by a bowl containing some red wine.

Boil the meat gently in this way for eight or nine hours, to obtain four or five spoonfuls of a reduced and flavorful broth which you will strain through a sieve, squeezing well, and which you will save for the next day.
Form the filling for the Anolini with: toasted breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, nutmeg scent, one egg and the meat broth. Make everything into a homogeneous mixture.

Make three sheets of pasta kept somewhat tender and fill the scalloped disc, folding it in two to obtain the shape of a small half moon. With this amount you will obtain about one hundred, which will be good in broth or dry like tortellini.
Cook the remaining meat alone or with a side of vegetables and it will be a stracotto.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arigusta (Lobster)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Fold the lobster's tail under and tie it before throwing it into boiling water
Flavor the water with a bundle made of onion, carrots, parsley and two bay leaves, adding two tablespoons of vinegar and a pinch of salt
Boil for 30 to 40 minutes depending on its size
Let the lobster cool in its broth
When removed, drain the water by squeezing the tail and after drying it, rub it with a few drops of oil to make it shiny
Send to table with an incision from head to tail to easily extract the flesh
Serve simply seasoned with oil and lemon juice, or accompanied with mayonnaise sauce or other spicy sauce

Alternatively serve with a sauce made as follows: extract the flesh from the head and mince it finely with a hard-boiled egg yolk and some parsley leaves, place the mixture in a sauce boat, season with pepper, little or no salt and dilute with fine oil and the juice of half a lemon, or vinegar

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Aringa Ingentilita (Refined Herring)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Open the herring from the back, remove the head and flatten it
Place in infusion in boiling milk and leave for eight to ten hours, changing the milk once if possible
Dry with a cloth
Cook on a grill like common herring
Season with oil and very little vinegar, or if preferred, with oil and lemon juice
Alternatively, place the herring on the fire with cold water, bring to boil for three minutes, then hold briefly in fresh water, dry it, remove the head, open from the back and season as above

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arista (Tuscan Roasted Pork Loin)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Lard the meat with garlic, bunches of rosemary, and a few cloves of garlic, but sparingly, as these are flavors that easily become overwhelming.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook it roasted on a spit, which is better, or send it to the oven without further ado.
Use the fat that it renders for browning potatoes or for making vegetable dishes.
Serve cold.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arnioni alla Parigina (Kidneys Parisian-Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one large or two small anchovies

steps: Take a veal kidney, remove the fat, open it and cover it with boiling water.
When the water has cooled, dry it well with a cloth and thread it lengthwise and crosswise with clean sticks so that it stays open (in Paris silver pins are used).
Season it with 30 grams of melted butter, salt and pepper, and leave it prepared this way for an hour or two.
Given that the kidney weighs 600 or 700 grams, take another 30 grams of butter and one large or two small anchovies and clean them.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arnioni alla Parigina (Veal Kidney Prepared in the Parisian Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one veal kidney (a piece of veal)
one large anchovy or two small anchovies

steps: Take a veal kidney, remove the fat, open it and cover it with boiling water.
When the water has cooled, dry it well with a cloth and skewer it lengthwise and crosswise with clean skewers so that it stays open (in Paris they use silver pins).
Season it with 30 grams of melted butter, salt and pepper, and let it sit prepared for one or two hours.

If the kidney weighs 600 or 700 grams, take another 30 grams of butter and one large anchovy or two small ones, clean them, chop them and crush them with the blade of a knife together with the butter and form them into a ball.
Cook the kidney on a grill, but not too much so that it remains tender, place it on a platter, spread it while hot with the ball of butter and anchovy and serve it to the table.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arnioni per Colazione (Kidneys for Breakfast)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: milk-fed veal, castrated lamb, pork or similar kidneys
five or six slices of bread marrow, dried by the heat

steps: Prepare a fine battutino (small chopped mixture) composed of parsley, half a clove of garlic, the juice of half a lemon and five or six slices of bread marrow, dried by the heat.
Open the kidneys to remove the fat and cut them into thin slices crosswise.
For a total of 400 or 500 grams, throw them in a pan with 50 to 60 grams of butter over high heat.
Move them often and as soon as they begin to brown add the battutino, season with salt and pepper and, always moving them with a spoon, pour in the lemon juice and finally a ladle of broth.
The operation should take about five minutes total and before serving pour them over the slices of bread.
This will be enough for four people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arnioni Saltati (Sautéed Kidneys)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one large animal kidney (or several from smaller animals)

steps: Open the kidney and remove all the fat as it has an unpleasant odor.
Cut it crosswise into thin slices, place in a bowl, salt it and pour over it enough boiling water to cover.
When the water has cooled, remove it dry and place in a pan to evaporate the water, which you will discard.
Sprinkle a pinch of flour over it, add a small piece of butter and, stirring often, let it grill for only five minutes.

Season with salt, pepper and a scant half glass of white wine, leave it briefly longer on the heat and when about to remove it add another small piece of butter, a pinch of chopped parsley and a bit of broth if needed.
Note: kidneys held too long on the heat become tough. It is good to boil the wine separately first until reduced by a third; if instead of white wine you use marsala or champagne, so much the better.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrostini di Vitella di Latte alla Salvia (Milk-Fed Veal Cutlets with Sage)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Milk-fed veal loin free of skin and with its bone attached, cut into thin scaloppine
Marsala wine, just under one finger (of a glass)

steps: Use a sauté pan or a copper skillet, and put it on the fire with some whole sage leaves and a proportioned piece of butter. When it has sautéed a little, throw in the scaloppine and while they brown over high heat, salt them on both sides, then sprinkle a little flour over them and finish cooking them with Marsala. They should remain with little moisture.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrosto d'Agnello all'Aretina (Lamb Roast Aretine Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: a leg or quarter of lamb

steps: Season the lamb with salt, pepper, oil and a drop of vinegar.
Pierce it here and there with the point of a knife and let it sit in this mixture for several hours.

Thread it onto the spit and frequently baste it with this liquid using a sprig of rosemary until cooked, which serves to remove any stable smell from the lamb, if you fear it has one, and to give it a pleasant taste.
If you prefer a more pronounced rosemary aroma, you can stud the piece with some sprigs of the same, removing them before serving at table.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrosto di Lepre I (Roasted Hare I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: half a glass of vinegar or less

steps: Infuse the hare for twelve to fourteen hours in a liquid prepared as follows: put on the fire three glasses of water with half a glass of vinegar or less in proportion to the size, three or four chopped shallots, one or two bay leaves, a small bunch of parsley, a bit of salt and a pinch of pepper; boil for five or six minutes and pour cold over the hare.
Remove from infusion and dry it well.
Stud it entirely with fine lardons using a larding needle.
Cook over gentle heat, salt sufficiently and baste with cream and nothing else.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrosto di Lepre II (Roasted Hare II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the thickest membranes from the external muscles.
Stud the entire piece with lardons of lard that you have salted beforehand.
Thread onto the spit, wrap it in buttered paper sprinkled with salt.
When cooked, remove the paper and brush with a sprig of rosemary dipped in butter, make it brown, salting it a bit more.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrosto di vitella di latte (Roasted Milk-Fed Veal)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: The pieces most suitable for roasting on a spit are the loin and the rump, and they need only oil and salt for seasoning.

These same pieces can also be cooked in a pan, lightly larded with garlic and rosemary, with oil, butter and a small amount of minced cured meat, salt, pepper and tomato juice, cooking fresh peas in the braising liquid.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrosto morto (Braised Veal)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: milk-fed veal, a nice piece from the loin including the stone

steps: Roll the meat and tie it with string so it stays together.
Place it in a pot with a small amount of fine oil and butter.
Brown it on all sides.
Salt it halfway through cooking and finish cooking it with broth so that little or no sauce remains.
If you do not have broth, use tomato juice or tomato paste dissolved in water.
If you like it more flavorful, add finely minced cured meat.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrosto morto coll'odore dell'aglio e del ramerino (Braised Veal with Garlic and Rosemary)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Prepare the veal as in the previous recipe for braising in a pot with oil and butter.
Instead of studding the meat with garlic and rosemary pieces, throw a whole clove of garlic and two sprigs of rosemary into the pot.
When you send the roast to the table, strain its reduced sauce without squeezing it and surround the meat with potatoes or vegetables cooked separately if you wish.
If you like, you can also enhance the meat with a very small amount of tomato juice or paste.
Lamb shanks are also very good prepared this way, cooked between two fires.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrosto morto coll'odore dell'aglio e del ramerino - Lamb Version (Braised Lamb Shanks with Garlic and Rosemary)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the lamb shanks between two fires following the method for braised veal with garlic and rosemary, placing whole garlic cloves and rosemary sprigs in the pot during cooking.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrosto Morto di Pollo alla Bolognese (Dead Roast Chicken Bologna Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: One slice of fat and lean prosciutto, finely minced
A few small pieces of garlic
Tomatoes in neat pieces without seeds, or tomato paste dissolved in water

steps: Place the chicken over the fire with oil, butter, finely minced fat and lean prosciutto, a few small pieces of garlic, and one small sprig of rosemary.
When it is browned, add tomatoes in neat pieces without seeds, or tomato paste dissolved in water.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove it and in that sauce cook potatoes cut into small pieces, then return the chicken to the fire to reheat it.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arrosto Morto Lardellato (Braised Larded Roast)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: a short, thick piece of lean veal or beef, from the thigh or rump, about one kilogram
30 grams of fat and lean ham cut into thin slices
one quarter of an onion divided into two pieces
three or four celery ribs less than a finger length
the same number of carrot strips

steps: Stud the meat with the ham slices using a larding needle.
Tie it with string to keep it compact and place it in a pot with butter, onion pieces, celery ribs and carrot strips.
Season with salt and pepper and when the meat has browned, turning it often, moisten with two small ladles of water.
Cook over gentle heat, allowing much of the moisture to reduce, but ensure it does not dry out and become black.
When serving, strain the small amount of remaining sauce and pour it over the meat, which can be surrounded with potato wedges browned in butter or oil.
Alternatively, you can put the braised roast on the fire with only butter and cook it in the covered pot with a bowl full of water placed on the lid.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Arselle o Telline alla Livornese (Mussels or Clams Livorno Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a fine mixture of onion and put it on the fire with oil and a pinch of pepper. When the onion has taken color, add a pinch of finely chopped parsley and shortly after add the clams or mussels with tomato juice or tomato paste. Shake them often and when they open, pour them over slices of toasted bread prepared beforehand on a platter.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Babà (Italian Sweet Yeast Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Hungarian flour or finest flour, 250 grams
Sultana raisins, also called currants, 50 grams
Malaga raisins with seeds removed, 30 grams
Milk or, better, cream, approximately 1 deciliter
Candied fruit cut into strips, 10 grams

steps: Mix the beer yeast with a quarter of the flour and a little of the lukewarm milk, and form a dough of appropriate consistency. Make a cross cut in the dough with a knife so that it shows the necessary swelling in time. Allow it to rise near the fire at very moderate heat, in a covered vessel with a drop of milk, which will take about half an hour.

While it rises, beat the eggs in a bowl with the sugar; then add the remaining flour, the risen small dough, the melted and lukewarm butter, the marsala and rum, and if the dough becomes too stiff, soften it with lukewarm milk. Work it thoroughly with a spoon until the mixture detaches from the bowl.
Finally add the raisins and candied fruit, and allow it to rise. When it has puffed up, stir it slightly with a spoon and pour it into a buttered mold dusted with powdered sugar mixed with flour.

The best mold form for this cake is copper with ribs; but note that it must be twice as large as the contents. Cover it with a lid so it does not get air and place it in a warm bath or inside a country oven, very slightly hot, to rise it; this will take perhaps more than two hours. If the rising is perfect you will see the mixture grow to double, that is, reach the mouth of the mold. Then bake it, taking care that it does not get air in the meantime. Doneness is tested by inserting a pomegranate stick which should come out dry; nevertheless leave it to dry further in the oven at moderate heat, which is necessary because of its thickness. When the Babà is turned out, if it is well baked, it should...

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Baccalà alla Bolognese (Salt Cod Bologna Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cut into pieces as large as the previous recipe and place raw in a pan or baking dish oiled
Sprinkle with a finely chopped mixture of garlic and parsley on top and season with pepper, oil and small pieces of butter
Cook over high heat and turn gently because, not being floured, it breaks easily
When cooked, squeeze lemon over it and serve

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Baccalà alla Fiorentina (Salt Cod Florentine Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: garlic cloves, whole and slightly crushed
tomato sauce or tomato conserve diluted in water

steps: Cut the salt cod into pieces as wide as the palm of your hand and flour well
Heat a pan or baking dish with considerable oil and two or three whole, slightly crushed garlic cloves over the fire
When the garlic begins to color, add the salt cod and brown on both sides, stirring often so it does not stick
Season with little to no salt (taste first) and a pinch of pepper
Finally pour a few spoonfuls of tomato sauce or diluted tomato conserve over it
Boil a little longer and serve

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Baccalà Dolce-Forte (Salt Cod Sweet and Sour)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook like salt cod recipe 506, without garlic, and when browned on both sides, pour the sweet-sour sauce over it
Boil a little longer and serve hot

For the sweet-sour sauce, prepare in advance in a glass: if the salt cod weighs about 500 grams, use one finger-length of strong vinegar, two finger-lengths of water, sugar to taste, pine nuts and raisins in proportion
It is good to boil this sauce separately a bit before pouring it over the salt cod

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Baccalà Fritto (Fried Salt Cod)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: To boil it, place in cold water over the fire and remove as soon as it reaches a boil, as it is then cooked
Without further handling it can be eaten seasoned with oil and vinegar
Alternatively, after boiling, place the whole piece of salt cod in infusion in red wine and keep for several hours
Dry in a cloth and cut

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Baccalà in Gratella (Salt Cod Grilled)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: To keep it less dry, cook slowly over a sheet of white paper, oiled beforehand
Season with oil, pepper and, if desired, a few small sprigs of rosemary

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Baccalà in Pastella (Salt Cod in Batter)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Boil the salt cod in cold water and remove it as soon as it reaches its first boil.
Place the whole piece of salt cod in an infusion of red wine and keep it there for several hours.
Dry it in a cloth and cut it into small pieces, cleaning it of bones and spines.
Lightly flour it and dip it into a simple batter made of water, flour, and a drop of oil without salt.
Fry it in oil and sprinkle it with sugar when it has lost its first boil.
Serve hot.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Baccalà in Salsa Bianca (Salt Cod in White Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Boil the salt cod and clean it of skin, spines, and bones.
Boil the potato and cut it into small pieces.
Make a béchamel sauce with the milk and flour.
When cooked, add some chopped parsley and flavor with nutmeg.
Pour in the potato pieces and salt.
Add the salt cod in pieces, mix well, and after a brief rest serve it.
Garnish with hard-boiled egg wedges if desired.
This quantity is sufficient for four people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Baccalà montebianco (Salt Cod Montebianco)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Clean the salt cod of its bones, small bones, skin and sinews, which present themselves like threads; this will leave approximately 340 grams of cleaned cod.
After having prepared it thus, pound it in a mortar and then place it in a small pot, together with the cream or milk, over a fire that is not too hot, stirring continuously.

When it has absorbed the cream or milk, begin to pour the oil drop by drop, as you would do for mayonnaise, always working it very much with the "wielded weapon", that is with the wooden spoon, so that it becomes refined and does not separate.
Remove it when it seems to you cooked to the point and serve it cold with a garnish of raw truffles cut into very thin slices, or with slices of fried bread, or caviar crostini.
This quantity can suffice for eight persons.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Balsamella (Béchamel Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Butter, the volume of an egg
Milk, half a liter of the best

steps: Put in a pan on the fire a tablespoon of flour and a piece of butter the volume of an egg.

Use a spoon to dissolve the butter and flour together and when this begins to take a hazelnut color, pour in half a liter of the best milk little by little, stirring continuously with the spoon until you see the liquid thickened like a cream of milky color.
This is the balsamella.
If it becomes too thick add milk, if too thin put it back on the fire with another small piece of butter mixed with flour.
The dose is abundant, but you can proportion it according to circumstances.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bastoncelli Croccanti (Crunchy Breadsticks)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a dough without stirring it too much.
Roll it out thin to obtain two dozen breadsticks ten centimeters long.
Bake them in a country oven on a baking sheet without any preparation.
They can be served with tea or with bottled wine.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bavarese lombarda (Bavarian Cream Lombard Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Butter of good quality and very fresh, 180 grams
Long savoiardi or sponge cake, approximately 150 grams
Vanilla sugar, enough to give it the flavor
Rosolio liqueur, as much as needed to lightly dip the savoiardi

steps: Boil the eggs for only seven minutes and remove the yolks, dissolve them in the butter, then pass them through a sieve, then add the powdered sugar and the vanilla sugar, and work the mixture well with a spoon to whip it

Take a mold, preferably one with ribs, dampen it with rosolio, cut in half lengthwise the savoiardi, dip them lightly in the rosolio, or half in rosolio and half in alkermes and with these line the mold alternating the two colors
Then pour the mixture in the middle, cover it with other savoiardi dipped in the same way, leave it in the ice for at least three hours and serve it
The mixture, if convenient, can be made a day ahead and this quantity is enough for eight people. It is a very refined pudding

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bianco Mangiare (Almond Blancmange)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Sweet almonds with three bitter almonds, 150 grams
Cream or milk, half a glass
Water, one and a half glasses

steps: First prepare the fish gelatin by pressing it with your fingers at the bottom of a glass, cover it with water and let it soften, then when you need it, discard the water and wash it

Shell and pound the almonds in a mortar, moistening them from time to time with a teaspoon of water, and when you have reduced them to a fine paste, dilute them with the aforementioned water and pass them through a strong, fine cloth, taking care to extract all the substance
At this point, prepare a mold of appropriate capacity
Then put on the fire in a pan the almond milk, the cream, the sugar, the gelatin, the orange blossom water; mix everything together and let it boil for a few minutes
Remove it from the fire and when it has cooled, pour it into the mold immersed in fresh water or ice
To unmold it, simply pass a cloth dampened in boiling water around the mold
Note: boiling is necessary so that the fish gelatin incorporates with the rest; otherwise it may precipitate to the bottom of the mold

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotti (Cookies)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a well in the mound of flour and place in it the aforementioned ingredients except the milk, which you will use to knead this dough, which should turn out soft and must be worked thoroughly to refine it
Then stretch out a sheet about one scudo thick, dusting it with flour if needed, and finally pass over it a ridged rolling pin, or use a grater or fork to make some decorations
After that, cut the cookies into whatever shape you prefer, or if you do not want to make long strips just slightly longer than a finger and two centimeters wide as I do
Place them directly in a copper baking pan and bake them in the oven or in a country oven

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotti Croccanti I (Crunchy Biscuits I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Sweet almonds, whole and blanched mixed with some pine nuts, 120 grams

steps: Set aside the almonds and pine nuts to add later.
Mix everything together with four eggs, keeping the fifth egg in reserve in case it is needed to form a somewhat soft dough.
Make four loaves the thickness of a finger and as wide as a hand.
Place them on a baking sheet buttered and floured, and gild them on top.
Do not bake them so much that they cannot be sliced, which will be better done the next day when the crust softens.
Put the slices back in the oven to toast them lightly on both sides, and you will have crunchy biscuits.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotti Croccanti II (Crunchy Biscuits II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: One whole egg and three yolks

steps: These biscuits are finer than the previous ones.
Blanch the almonds, and leave both these and the pine nuts whole.
Cut the candied fruit into small pieces.
Make a well in the mound of flour and place the eggs, sugar, butter, spirits, and baking soda in it.
Mix the dough without working it too much, then open it and spread it to add the rest.
Roll out a somewhat compressed stick about one meter long, divide it into four or five parts so it fits in the baking sheet.
Gild it and bake it in the oven.
Once baked, cut it in the shape of biscuits into slices slightly thicker than one centimeter.
Toast them lightly on both sides.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotti da Famiglia (Family Biscuits)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a well in the mound of flour and place the ingredients listed above except the milk, which you will use to mix this dough, which should be soft and must be stirred well to refine it.
Roll out a sheet about the thickness of a scudo coin, dusting it with flour if necessary.
Finally pass a notched rolling pin over it, or use a grater or a fork to make some decoration.
Cut the biscuits in the shape you prefer.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotti della Salute (Health Cookies)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Mix the sugar with the flour, make a well in it to place the rest and knead it with the addition of a little milk to obtain a somewhat soft dough, which you will shape into a slightly flattened cylindrical form about half a meter long
To bake it in the oven or country oven, butter a baking pan, and since this stick must fit in it, divide it into two pieces, keeping them separate as they will puff up greatly
The next day, cut them into cookie shapes, from which you will get about thirty, and toast them

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotti Teneri (Soft Biscuits)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Blanch the almonds, cut them in half crosswise and dry them in the sun or by the fire.
Cut the candied fruit and preserve, which may be quince or other firm fruit, into small dice.
Work the egg yolks with the sugar and a little of the flour for more than half an hour.
Add the stiffly beaten egg whites and after mixing them in, add the flour, letting it fall from a small sieve.
Mix gently and scatter the almonds, candied fruit, and preserve into the dough.
Butter a tin box and dust it with flour.
Cut the biscuits the next day, toasting them on both sides if you like.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscottini Puerperali (Puerperal Biscuits)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Vanilla flavoring by means of vanilla sugar

steps: Place these ingredients in a vessel and work them with a spoon for over a quarter of an hour
Then pour the mixture into four paper boxes, approximately eight centimeters long and six centimeters wide

Place them in a covered copper baking pan, set it over a burner with very little fire underneath and on top so the mixture firms up somewhat without forming a crust, as it must be taken up in spoonfuls
Therefore the name biscottini is quite improper

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotto (Sponge Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Work for at least half an hour the egg yolks with the sugar and one tablespoon of the said flours, using a spoon. Beat the egg whites until very stiff and add them; mix gently and, when they are blended together, let the two flours fall from a small sieve, which you will have dried in the sun or over heat beforehand.
Bake it in the oven or country oven in a pan where it comes up about three fingers high, but first grease it with cold butter and dust it with powdered sugar mixed with flour.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotto alla Sultana (Sultan's Cookie)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: First place on the fire the raisins and candied fruit cut to the size of watermelon seeds with enough cognac or rum to cover them; when this boils, ignite it and let it burn outside the fire until the liquor is consumed; then remove this mixture and let it dry among the folds of a towel
After this operation, work very well with a wooden spoon for half an hour the sugar and egg yolks where you have placed the lemon zest

Beat the egg whites until stiff with a whisk, and pour them into the mixture; then add the two flours letting them fall through a small sieve and at the same time mix slowly and gently so that everything combines well, without working it too much
Finally add the raisins, candied fruit and the two tablespoons of rum or cognac mentioned and pour the mixture into a smooth mold or in a copper pot that gives the dessert a tall and round shape

Butter the mold and dust it with powdered sugar and flour, being careful to put it in the oven immediately to prevent the raisins and candied fruit from sinking to the bottom. If this happens, another time leave out one egg white
Serve cold

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotto da Servirsi con lo Zabaione (Cake to Serve with Zabaglione)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: First work the egg yolks with the sugar for almost half an hour, add the well-beaten egg whites and let the flour fall from a sifter, mixing everything nicely so that the mixture remains light
Pour it into a ring mold that you have first buttered and dusted with flour and powdered sugar
Put it immediately in the oven to cook, and once cooled and unmolded, pour the zabaglione from recipe 684 into the hole and send it immediately to the table
This is a dose that can serve five or six people

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Biscotto di Cioccolata (Chocolate Sponge Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Grate the chocolate and put it in a bowl with the sugar and egg yolks and beat them with a spoon; then add the flour and work the mixture for more than half an hour; finally the beaten egg whites mixing gently.
Bake it as the previous recipe.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bistecca alla Fiorentina (Florentine-Style Steak)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: beef steak from the loin, thick as one or one and a half fingers

steps: Place the steak on the grill over hot charcoal, either natural as it comes from the animal or at most washed and dried.
Turn it several times and season with salt and pepper when it is cooked.
Send it to table with a small piece of butter on top.
It should not be too cooked because its beauty is that when you cut it, it releases abundant juice on the plate.
Do not salt it before cooking because the heat will dry it, and if you season it beforehand with oil or other things, as many do, it will taste rancid and be nauseating.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bistecca nel Tegame (Steak in the Pan)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: If you have a large steak that, for being from an animal not very young or not recently slaughtered, makes you doubt its tenderness, instead of cooking it on the grill, place it in a pan with a piece of butter and a little oil.
Proceed as indicated, give it the flavor of garlic and rosemary.

Add, if necessary, a little broth or water, or tomato juice and serve it at table with potatoes cut into chunks cooked in its gravy, and if that is not enough, add more broth, butter and tomato preserves.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bocca di Dama I (Lady's Mouth I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Mandorle dolci con alcune amare, 50 grammi

steps: Le mandorle, dopo averle sbucciate e asciugate bene, pestatele in un mortaio con una cucchiaiata del detto zucchero e mescolatele alla farina in modo che non appariscano bozzoli
Il resto dello zucchero ponetelo in una catinella coi rossi d'uovo e la raschiatura del limone, lavorandoli con un mestolo per un quarto d'ora
Versate la farina e lavorate ancora per più di mezz'ora

Montate con la frusta, in un vaso a parte, le sei chiare e quando saranno ben sode da sostenere un pezzo da due lire d'argento, versatele nella menzionata catinella e mescolate adagino adagino ogni cosa insieme
Versatela in una teglia di rame unta col burro e spolverizzata di zucchero a velo e farina, oppure in un cerchio di legno da staccio il cui fondo sia stato chiuso con un foglio
Cuocete in forno

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bocca di Dama II (Lady's Mouth II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Mandorle dolci con tre amare, 50 grammi

steps: Sbucciate le mandorle, asciugatele bene al sole o al fuoco, pestatele finissime con una cucchiaiata del detto zucchero e mescolatele alla farina
Il resto dello zucchero e i rossi delle uova uniteli insieme in una bacinella di rame o di ottone, e sopra al fuoco, a poco calore, batteteli colla frusta per più di un quarto d'ora
Versateci poscia, fuori del fuoco, la farina preparata con le mandorle, la scorza di limone grattata
Dopo averla lavorata ancora, aggiungete le chiare ben montate e mescolate adagio
Ponete il composto in una teglia unta col burro e spolverizzata di farina mista con zucchero a velo
Mandatela in forno

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bocconi di Pane Ripieni (Stuffed Bread Morsels)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: chicken or turkey gizzard, if available

steps: If using gizzards, boil them first until half-cooked and remove the tender parts.
Mince all the organ meats, put them in a pan with a battuto of onion, prosciutto, and butter, and season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg or spices.
When it begins to brown, sprinkle in a scant teaspoon of flour, mix to incorporate, and moisten with meat gravy or broth.
Boil, then gradually add beaten egg while stirring constantly until the mixture sets.
Remove from heat, add a pinch of parmesan cheese, and pour into a dish.
Cut stale bread into thick slices about one centimeter, remove the crust, and cut into cubes about the size of a 10-centimeter coin.
Mound the filling generously on one side of each bread cube and half an hour before frying, dust with flour and spread on a tray.
Generously pour beaten egg over them so the bread absorbs it and the filling remains covered and well-coated.
Fry in a pan, starting with the filling side down.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bombe Composte (Composed Cheese and Mortadella Puffs)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Put water on the fire with butter and salt
When it begins to boil, throw in the cheese in small pieces and immediately all the flour at once, stirring vigorously
Keep the paste on the fire about 10 minutes, stirring always, then let it cool
Work it much and in stages with a spoon, adding one egg at a time, first the yolk then the beaten white
When about to fry it, add the mortadella in dice about one centimeter wide
If the mixture turns out a bit too firm due to the flour quality or because the eggs were small, add another egg
You will obtain enough for six people
If these puffs turn out well, you will see them puff up and remain empty inside
Serve hot as a side to fried meat or liver, or mixed with any other fried dish

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bombe di Semolino (Semolina Puffs)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Put milk on the fire with butter and sugar
When it begins to boil, add the semolina little by little so it does not form lumps
Keep it on the fire until well firm, stirring always with a spoon so it does not stick to the bottom
Remove from the fire, salt it and immediately break in the first egg, then when about to fry it, add the other two, one at a time, beating the whites and working it always much with the spoon
When you throw it in the pan, give it the shape of small balls which will puff up to become very light puffs
Dust with powdered sugar once they have lost their strong heat
Use gentle fire and shake the pan

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bombe e Pasta Siringa (Choux Puffs and Piped Paste)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Fine Hungarian or finest flour, 100 grams

steps: Put water, butter, and salt on the fire
When it boils, add all the flour at once and stir vigorously
Keep the paste on the fire until the flour is well cooked (10 minutes), stirring constantly
Remove from the pot and flatten to the thickness of a finger so it cools well
Begin working it early with an egg yolk; when it is incorporated, add a well-beaten egg white
Add another yolk and, working always with a spoon, another beaten egg white, and so on if the dose were double or triple the present one
By dint of working it, the mixture must turn out fine as an ointment in the end
If making puffs, drop by spoonfuls into a pan giving them round shape
If desiring piped paste, pass it through a piping bag with a stellate disc and cut to a length of 9 to 10 centimeters
When it has lost its first heat, dust with powdered sugar
This dose will serve eight or ten people when doubled or tripled
These puffs can also serve as a composed fried dish by making a small incision when cooked to introduce inside a little delicate minced meat; but then do not dust with sugar

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bracioline alla Bartola (Braised Veal Rolls, Bartola Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: veal or beef meat (fillet, round, rump, or leg), net weight without bone, 500 grams
one rib of celery, about one hand's length

steps: Cut the meat into thick slices, almost a finger thick, to obtain no more than seven or eight braised rolls to which you endeavor to give a nice shape, and beat them with the back of a knife.

Make a mixture minced very finely with the prosciutto and the ingredients described above, then pour six tablespoons of oil in a sauté pan or copper pan on which, when cold, you will place the braised rolls spreading on each one a pinch of the said mixture.

Season them with little salt, pepper and only the flower of four or five cloves, and over high heat brown them from underneath, then turn them one by one with its mixture to brown this as well, and when it has softened sufficiently turn them back over so the mixture returns to the top picking up what has remained stuck to the pan, then bathe them with tomato juice or preserve dissolved in water, cover them and let them boil slowly for almost two hours; but half an hour before sending them to the table cook in the sauce of the same a large peeled potato and cut into ten or twelve pieces placing them in the spaces between one braised roll and the other.
It would be better to send them to the table in the vessel where they have been cooked; but if this is unseemly place them as they are in a serving dish with the potatoes around them.
This quantity is enough for four or five people, and it is not a dish to be despised, because it does not leave the stomach burdened.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bracioline alla Contadina (Veal Rolls Peasant Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water

steps: Prepare the veal rolls with well-beaten lean veal, oil them and season with salt and pepper.
Make a mixture of olives in brine, capers squeezed of vinegar and one anchovy, chopping everything finely.
Leave it simple, or add an egg yolk and a pinch of parmesan.
Fill the rolls with this mixture, tie them, and cook them with butter and tomato juice, or in an onion soffritto.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bracioline di Vitella di Latte all'Uccelletto (Veal Scallops, Little Bird Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Pound the veal scallops well with the back of a knife blade.
Heat oil and butter in a saucepan or sauté pan with whole sage leaves and let them soften slightly.
Add the veal scallops, season with salt and pepper, and boil over high heat for five or six minutes.
Squeeze lemon juice over them and serve.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bracioline Ripiene (Stuffed Braised Veal Rolls)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: lean veal or milk-fed veal meat, 70 grams

steps: From the braised rolls you will obtain 6 or 7 if you keep them as wide as a hand: beat them very well with a meat beater or with the handle of a knife dipped often in water to widen them.

Then mince finely the prosciutto with 70 grams of the second meat and to this mixture unite the Parmesan and the marrow first made pasty with the blade of a knife; lastly add the egg to bind the mixture and a pinch of pepper, salt not being necessary because of the prosciutto and Parmesan.
Spread out the braised rolls and on the middle of them distribute the said mixture; then roll them up and tie them crosswise with twine.

Now that they have already taken the required form, prepare a light mixture with a little onion, a small piece of white celery, a small piece of carrot and 20 grams of dried meat, and place it on the fire in a saucepan with 20 grams of butter, at the same time as you place the braised rolls.
Season them with salt and pepper, and when they have taken on color pour tomato juice or preserve and finish cooking them with water.
You can also add, if you like, a drop of white wine.
When you send them to the table remove the twine with which you had tied them.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bracioline ripiene con carciofi (Braised Veal or Beef Rolls Stuffed with Artichokes)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: slice of fatty and lean prosciutto

steps: Remove all the tough leaves from the artichokes and cut them into four or five wedges.
Take a slice of fatty and lean prosciutto and chop it very finely, mix it with a little butter and spread this mixture over the artichoke wedges.

Pound and flatten the bracioline, which can be of veal or beef, season them with salt and pepper and place two or three of the prepared artichoke wedges in the middle of each one, then roll them up and tie them with string in a cross pattern.
Make a battutino with a little onion, put it in a pot with butter and oil and when the onion is well browned place the bracioline in it and season them again with salt and pepper.
Brown them, then finish cooking them with tomato juice or tomato paste dissolved in water, and when you serve them remove the string.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Braciuola di Manzo alla Sautè o in Teglia (Beef Braciole, Sautéed or in a Pan)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Beat it very well with the back of a knife.
Put it on the fire with a piece of butter proportioned to its size.
Season it with salt and pepper.
Turn it often so it browns on both sides.
When it has absorbed almost all the butter, moisten it twice with a few drops of water.
When cooked, sprinkle a pinch of chopped parsley over it.
Keep it on the fire for another moment and serve it with its sauce.
You can garnish it with fried potatoes if you like.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Braciuola di Manzo Ripiena Arrosto (Roasted Stuffed Beef Roulade)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: One beef cutlet, the thickness of a finger, weighing about 500 grams
One ball of fresh bread crumb about the size of a fist

steps: Make a fine mixture with onion the size of a walnut, a little celery, carrot and parsley; put it on the fire with the said butter and, once browned, throw in the milk veal in pieces and the livers, a little salt and pepper for seasoning, cooking the meat with a little broth.
Remove it dry to mince it finely with the mezzaluna and in the remaining liquid make a thick paste with the bread crumb, moistening it with broth if needed.
Now make a single mixture with the minced meat, the paste, the egg, the Parmesan, the prosciutto and the tongue cut into dice.
Once the filling is composed this way, just dip the beef cutlet in water to be able to stretch it better, beat it with the back of the knife blade and flatten it with the blade.
Place the filling in the middle and form a roll that you will tie tightly like a salami first from the long side and then crosswise.
Thread it onto the spit along its length and roast it with oil and salt.
You will have a delicate roast which can serve six or seven people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Braciuola Ripiena (Stuffed Braised Meat Roll)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one large thin sheet of meat for braising
chicken breast, cut into fillets thicker than one centimeter

steps: Cut the chicken breast and the mortadella and prosciutto slices into thick fillets.
Spread some of the prepared filling mixture on the meat sheet.
Arrange a third of the fillets on top, interspersing them, and spread more filling over them.
Repeat this layering process two more times.
Roll the meat sheet tightly around the filling (like a salami roll) and tie it securely with kitchen twine.
Heat 30 grams of butter in a pot and brown the roll, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Once browned, pour off the fat (which can be saved for other dishes).
Continue cooking for approximately three hours, adding broth gradually as needed.
Once cooled, remove the twine, slice into portions, and serve.
Serves 10 to 12 people, especially when garnished with meat gelatin.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Braciuole di castrato e filetto di vitella alla finanziera (Braised Mutton and Veal Fillet in Financier Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: whole braciuole of mutton from the loin

steps: Place a slice of prosciutto at the bottom of a pot with some butter, a small bundle made of carrot, celery and parsley stems, and on top of these place whole braciuole of mutton from the loin, which you will season with salt and pepper.

Brown them on both sides, add another piece of butter if needed, and add to the braciuole chicken gizzards and then livers, sweetbreads and fresh or dried mushrooms (already softened), all cut into pieces.
When these ingredients have also taken color, moisten with broth and cook over low heat.

Bind the sauce with a little flour, and lastly pour in half a glass, or even less, of good white wine, first reduced by half in a separate vessel over the fire, and let it boil a little longer so that it incorporates.
When ready to serve, remove the prosciutto and the bundle, strain the sauce through a colander and degrease it.
The same method can be used for a piece of veal fillet instead of mutton, adding peas to the ingredients mentioned.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Braciuole nella Scamerita (Pork Rolls in Pork Belly)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Place the rolls in a pan with very little oil, two or three cloves of garlic with their skin, slightly crushed, and season with salt and pepper.
When they have taken color on both sides, pour two or three fingers of a glass of red wine into the pan and let it reduce by half as it boils.
Set the rolls aside dry, keeping them warm.
In that liquid, adjust the seasoning of the blanched kale, pressed of water, cut not too finely and also seasoned with salt and pepper.
Serve at table with the kale underneath.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Brigidini (Tuscan Waffle Cookies)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a rather firm paste, work it with your hands on a work surface and form small balls about the size of a small walnut.
Place them in the waffle iron on a waffle mold at a proper distance from one another and, turning the iron back and forth over the hot flame with wood fire, remove them when they have taken color.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Brioches
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Dissolve the beer yeast with lukewarm water in one quarter of the said flour; form it into a round small loaf of proper consistency, make a cross cut in it and place it to rise in a warm place inside a small copper pot with a veil of flour underneath

To the remaining flour make a well in the middle, place in it the sugar, salt and one egg, and with your fingers combine these three things together, then add the butter in small pieces and begin to knead the flour, first using the blade of a knife and then your hands, to form a dough which you will place in a bowl to work it better
Unite to this the risen small loaf, when it has grown double in size, and using your hand to work it a lot, add the other eggs one at a time

Then place the bowl in a warm and well-closed place, and when the dough has risen, spread it out somewhat and with it fill halfway about twenty buttered metal molds with ridges, which beforehand you will have buttered with liquid butter or lard and dusted with flour mixed with powdered sugar
Return them to rise, then glaze them and bake them in the oven or country oven

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Broccoli o talli di rape alla fiorentina (Broccoli or Turnip Greens Florentine-Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Clean the broccoli from the hardest leaves, boil them, squeeze out the water and cut them roughly.
Mince two or three garlic cloves or leave them whole, and once they have taken color with abundant oil in a pan, add the broccoli.
Season with salt and pepper, stir often and let them fry well.
They can be served as a side dish to boiled meat or eaten alone.
If you prefer, boil them and season with oil and vinegar.
In countries where oil is not perfect, you can substitute with lard; in fact, to my taste, fried with this they are better.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Broccoli romani (Roman Broccoli)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: lardo vergine or strutto (pure lard or lard)

steps: Clean them from the hardest leaves and boil them. Remove from boiling water and place them in cold water, and after squeezing well, cut them roughly and place them in a pan with virgin lard, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Once it has absorbed all the fat, sprinkle with sweet white wine, continue to drag them in the pan until it has been completely absorbed and evaporated, then serve as they will be praised.
For another method of cooking these broccoli without boiling them first: use only the flower and the most tender leaves; cut these roughly and the flower into small pieces.
Put the pan on the fire with oil in proportion and one garlic clove cut into thin slices lengthwise.

When the garlic begins to brown, add the leaves and then the flower raw in the pan, salt and pepper for seasoning, and as they dry by boiling, stirring always, wet them with a drop of hot water and, almost when cooking is complete, with white wine.
Since I cannot give you the precise amounts of this dish, have the patience to make some trials (I make many!) to ascertain its best taste.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Brodo (Broth)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lean veal or beef cut into thin slices

steps: Cut lean veal or beef into thin slices and arrange them one on top of the other in a wide pan
Salt them somewhat and pour over them enough cold water so that they are submerged
Cover the pan with a plate that closes it securely

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino alla Genovese (Genoese Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Mince the veal, chicken breast, and prosciutto with a crescent-shaped knife. Place them in a mortar with the butter, Parmesan, a piece of bread crumb soaked in milk, and pound thoroughly until it can be passed through a sieve.
Place the sieved mixture in a bowl and add three tablespoons of béchamel (made to the consistency of a paste for this dish), the eggs, and nutmeg. Mix well.
Butter a smooth tin mold and place a sheet of buttered paper cut to size at the bottom. Pour in the mixture and cook in a bain-marie.
