After unmolding, remove the paper and spread on that spot a sauce made from minced chicken liver cooked in broth.
Serve hot. If well made, it will be praised for its delicacy.
This serves six people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino alla Napoletana (Neapolitan Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Short pastry crust, half the amount of recipe N. 589A
Fruit preserves of various kinds such as raspberry, quince, apricot, etc.

steps: Cook the semolina in three glasses of milk, taking care that it does not become too firm
Remove from heat and season it with sugar, a pinch of salt and lemon zest; when it is no longer boiling, add three egg yolks and two egg whites, mixing everything well
Take a medium-sized copper baking dish, butter or lard it, and line it with a sheet of short pastry crust about half a scudo thick
Pour one third of the semolina into the dish and scatter over it, at some distance from one another, small pieces or spoonfuls of various fruit preserves such as raspberry, quince, apricots, etc.
Place a second and third layer on top of this first layer, always adorning them with the said preserves
Cover the top of the pudding with a sheet of the same pastry and moisten the edges with a finger dipped in water so that they stick together
Make some decorative marks, brush it with egg yolk and cook it in the oven
When you unmold it, dust it with powdered sugar and serve it cold
The preserves can be replaced with sultana raisins and candied fruit cut into pieces

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino alla Tedesca (German-Style Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: If you can find bread in loaf form, English style, use this as it is better than any other. Crumble or slice the bread crumb and soak it with ice-cold milk. When well soaked, squeeze it out with a cloth and pass it through a sieve. In winter, melt the butter in a bain-marie and work it with a wooden spoon together with the egg yolks until they are incorporated; add the whites, the bread crumb and the sugar and stir again. Pour the mixture into a mold greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs and cook it like the other puddings; that is in the oven. If you do it with care it will come out looking fine and tasting delicate. Serve hot.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di Cervelli di Maiale (Pork Brain Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Heat the brains with the butter, salt them, and cook, stirring often to prevent sticking, without browning them. Pass them through a sieve.
Add the Parmesan, nutmeg, beaten eggs, and cream. Mix well.
Pour the mixture into a smooth mold buttered with cold butter and cook in a bain-marie.
This is almost better cold than hot and serves six people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di Cioccolata (Chocolate Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Grate the chocolate, put it in the milk and when this begins to boil throw in the sugar and the ladyfingers, crumbling them with your fingers
Stir from time to time, so that the mixture does not stick to the bottom and after half an hour of boiling pass it through a sieve
When it is cold add the beaten eggs and the vanilla, pour it into a smooth mold, the bottom of which you will have first covered with a layer of liquefied sugar, and cook it in a bain-marie
50 grams of sugar are sufficient to cover the bottom of the mold
Serve cold

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di farina di riso (Rice Flour Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: First dissolve the flour with a quarter of the milk cold
Add some of the hot milk when it is boiling and pour it into the rest of the milk when it boils; this will prevent lumps from forming
When it is cooked add the sugar, butter, and salt
Remove it from the fire and wait until it is lukewarm to mix in the eggs and flavoring
Cook this pudding like the previous one

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di Limone (Lemon Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Sweet almonds with three bitter almonds, 170 grams
One teaspoon of rum or cognac

steps: Cook the lemon in water, for which two hours will be sufficient
Remove it dry and pass it through a sieve
However, before passing it taste it, because if it tasted too bitter you would need to keep it in fresh water until it had lost that unpleasant flavor
Add to it the sugar, the blanched and very finely pounded almonds, the six egg yolks and the rum
Mix everything well, beat the six egg whites and add them to the mixture which you will pour into a mold to cook it in the stove or in the oven
It can be served either hot or cold

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di Mandorle Tostate (Roasted Almond Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: First prepare the almonds, that is blanch them in hot water and roast them on the fire over a stone or iron slab; then pound them reducing them almost to powder and, putting the mixture on the fire without the eggs, add the almonds to it and after a short cooking pass it through a sieve
Now add the beaten eggs and set it in a bain-marie with a layer of melted sugar on the bottom of the mold
No flavoring is needed
The roasting of the almonds will give this pudding a grayish color and will give it a flavor so pleasant as to deserve the praise of men and even more that of women of delicate taste

Both this and the chocolate pudding can be put on ice before serving them, and also, to give them a more beautiful appearance, they can be covered with a cream adorned with colored confetti, or with whipped cream

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di Nocciuole (Hazelnut Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Blanch the hazelnuts in hot water and dry them well in the sun or by the fire.
Then pound them very finely in a mortar with the sugar poured in little by little.
Put the milk on the fire and when it comes to a boil, crumble the savoiardi biscuits into it and let them boil for five minutes, adding the butter.
Strain the mixture through a sieve and put it back on the fire with the pounded hazelnuts to dissolve the sugar.
Let it cool, then add the eggs, first the yolks, then the whites beaten stiff.
Pour it into a mold buttered and dusted with breadcrumbs, not filling it completely.
Bake it in the oven or in a cooking stove and serve it cold.
This quantity will serve nine or ten people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di Pane e Cioccolata (Bread and Chocolate Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Pour hot milk over bread cut into thin slices
After about two hours of steeping, pass it through a sieve to make it uniform
Put it on the fire with the sugar, butter, and grated chocolate
Stir the mixture frequently, let it boil somewhat and let it cool
Add the eggs, first the yolks and then the whipped whites
Cook it in a bain-marie in a smooth buttered mold and serve it cold
For better appearance, it would be good to cover it after unmolding with a cream
This dose will be sufficient for five people

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di Patate (Potato Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the potatoes in water or steamed, peel them and pass them hot through a sieve. Put them back on the fire with the butter, flour and milk, poured in little by little, working them well with a wooden spoon; then add the sugar, salt and flavoring and let them rest until all these things are well incorporated together.
Remove from the fire; when they are lukewarm or cold, add the yolks and then the beaten whites.
Cook it like all the other puddings; that is in the oven or in the stove and serve it hot.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di Ricotta (Ricotta Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Sweet almonds, 100 grams and three or four bitter almonds

steps: Blanch the almonds in hot water and pound them very finely in a mortar with one of the egg whites mentioned above
Mix them well with the ricotta, passing the ricotta first through a sieve if it were too hard or lumpy
Add the sugar and the eggs after having beaten them separately and pour the mixture into a pudding mold that you will have first buttered and sprinkled with breadcrumbs
Cook it in the oven or between two fires in a stove and serve it cold

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di Riso (Rice Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Eggs, two whole and two yolks
Rum or cognac, one small glass

steps: Cook the rice well in the milk and at half cooking throw into it the sugar, the currants, the candied fruit cut into very small pieces, a pinch of salt, and butter about the size of an egg minus a little. When cooked, remove it from the fire and while still hot, but not boiling, add the eggs, the rum and the vanilla, mixing everything well. Then pour it into a pudding mold well greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs; cook it in the oven or on the stove and serve it hot.
Set aside a third of the milk to add as needed as the rice thickens.
Will be enough for eight people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di semolino (Semolina Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Prepare the mixture and remove it from the fire
Cook it in a smooth or worked mold, first greased with butter and dusted with breadcrumbs
If a common or country oven is lacking, puddings can also be cooked well in a hearth burner
Serve this pudding hot

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino di semolino e conserve (Semolina Pudding with Preserves)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the semolina in the milk
Add the sugar and butter when it is boiling
Add the flavoring and salt when you remove it from the fire
Beat the eggs when it is still hot and mix very well
Prepare a pudding mold, smooth or worked, greased with butter and sprinkled with breadcrumbs

Pour the mixture into it little by little while cold, decorating it gradually with preserves in pieces or by spoonfuls according to whether they are liquid or solid; however, be warned that they should not touch the walls of the mold, as they would stick to them, and that there should not be too much of them, as they would become cloying
Serve it hot after cooking it on the hearth
The preserves that, to my taste, are most suited for this sweet are those of raspberry and quince; but those of apricots, currants, and peaches can also be used
For eight or ten persons, double the dose

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino Gabinetto (Cabinet Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Boil the milk for half an hour with the sugar in it
Remove the seeds from the Malaga raisins; cut the candied fruit into small cubes and likewise the preserves, if they were firm, which in this case would be better
Burn the grapes and candied fruit with rum as in the Biscotto alla Sultana N.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Budino Nero (Black Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Blanch the almonds, dry them well in the sun or by the fire, chop them with a mincing knife and put them on the fire in a saucepan when the sugar is dissolved
After the mixture has taken on the color of brittle, or the color of almond skin, pour it into a mortar and, once cooled, reduce it to powder
Mix this powder with the six beaten egg whites, put the mixture in a mold buttered with only cold butter and cook it in a bain-marie to serve it cold

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bue alla Brace (Braised Beef)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 500 grams lean and tender beef without bone
50 grams lard cut into thick strips about a finger's length
one quarter of a medium onion
one celery rib about a palm's length
vegetables for garnish such as spinach, Brussels sprouts, carrots, fennel

steps: Lard the meat with the lard strips seasoned with salt and pepper
Make a battuto (soffritto) with the onion, carrot, and celery, chopping it coarsely
Place the battuto in a pot with 30 grams of butter and put the tied and seasoned meat on top
When the battuto is nearly consumed, wet it twice with a bit of cold water
Once the meat is colored and the battuto consumed, pour in two ladles of hot water
Cover the pot with double paper and let it boil slowly until the meat is cooked
Strain the sauce, remove the fat, and return it to the fire with another piece of butter
Season the sauce to taste and serve with a garnish of vegetables of your choice

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bue alla California (Californian-Style Beef)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 700 grams lean beef without bone from the rump, loin, or fillet
1 tablespoon strong vinegar or more if weak
half an onion cut into four wedges

steps: Place the meat in a pot with the butter, onion wedges, carrot pieces, salt and pepper
When the meat is well browned, pour in the vinegar
After some time, add the water
Then add the cream
Let it boil slowly for about three hours, adding more water if the sauce becomes scarce
Serve the meat sliced with its sauce strained through a sieve
This dish can serve five or six people as one of several courses

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bue alla Moda (Braised Beef)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Not less than 1 kilogram of lean meat from the hip or rump of beef
Thick lardoon strips, wrapped in salt and pepper
Half a calf's foot or a piece of a large calf's foot
1 bunch tied of aromatic herbs such as parsley, celery, basil and the like
1 bold glass of water or better 1 glass of degreased broth
Half a glass of white wine or 2 tablespoons of brandy

steps: Take not less than 1 kilogram of lean meat from the hip or rump of beef and lard it with thick lardoon strips wrapped in salt and pepper
Tie the piece of meat so it takes a nice shape, salt it sufficiently
Place it in a braising pan with 50 grams of butter to brown it

Add the following ingredients: half a calf's foot or a piece of a large calf's foot, 1 large whole onion, 2 or 3 whole carrots, 1 bunch tied of aromatic herbs such as parsley, celery, basil and the like, some lardoon rinds, 1 glass of water or better 1 glass of degreased broth, and finally half a glass of white wine or 2 tablespoons of brandy
Put the well-covered pan on the fire and simmer slowly until the meat is cooked
Remove the carrots early so they remain whole
Discard the aromatic bunch, strain the sauce and degrease if necessary
Serve the meat not overcooked, surrounded by the carrots cut into round slices

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Bue Garofanato (Beef with Cloves)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: A nice piece of lean beef from the thigh or rump, about 1 kilogram
Butter and oil in equal quantities

steps: Take a fine piece of lean from the thigh or rump, beat it, and place it in wine to soak the evening for the following morning. Given that the piece is about one kilogram, lard it with lardons and four cloves, tie it and put it on the fire with half an onion cut into thin slices, butter and oil in equal quantities and salt it. Brown it on all sides and render the onion, pour a glass of water and, covering the mouth of the pot with a sheet of paper in two or three layers held firm by the lid, let it boil gently until cooked. Release it and serve it with its sauce all around, strained and degreased. The lardons of lard, as I have told you other times, it is good to keep them the thickness of a finger and season them with salt and pepper.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cacciucco I (Tuscan Fish Stew)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 300 grams of tomatoes, in pieces, or tomato paste

steps: Finely chop half an onion and put it to fry gently with oil, parsley and two whole cloves of garlic.
As soon as the onion has taken on color, add 300 grams of tomatoes in pieces, or tomato paste, and season with salt and pepper.
Once the tomatoes are cooked, pour over them one finger of vinegar if it is strong, or two if it is weak, diluted in a good glass of water.
Let it boil for a few more minutes, then remove the garlic and pass the rest through a sieve, pressing well.

Put the strained liquid back on the fire, together with the fish you have ready, such as sole, red mullet, scorpionfish, dogfish, gobies, mantis shrimp, and other seasonal varieties, leaving small fish whole and cutting large ones into pieces.
Taste to see if the seasoning is right; but in any case it will not hurt to add a little oil, keeping rather sparing with the initial frying.

When the fish is cooked and the cacciucco is made, it is customary to bring it to the table in two separate serving dishes; in one the fish alone, in the other as many slices of bread, thick as a finger, as the remaining broth can soak, but first dry them by the fire without toasting them.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cacciucco II (Lighter Tuscan Fish Stew)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one glass of liquid composed of one third dry white wine or red wine and the rest water

steps: Pound in a mortar three large cloves of garlic and fresh or dried ginger, reducing it to powder.

Put this mixture on the fire in a terracotta pan or pot with oil in proportion, and when it has fried gently, pour in a glass of liquid made up of one third dry white wine or red wine and the rest water.
Place the fish in it, salt it and shortly after add tomato juice or tomato paste dissolved in a drop of water.
Boil over a strong fire, always keeping the pot covered, never touch the fish so as not to break it, and you will find it cooked in a few minutes.
Serve it as the previous one, with slices of bread set apart which you will dry first by the fire without toasting them.
If the fish, before cooking it, remains raw for several hours, it keeps better if salted; but then it is well to wash it before putting it on the fire.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cacimperio (Cheese Fondue)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Fontina cheese, trimmed of rind, 400 grams

steps: Cut the Fontina into small dice and keep it soaking in milk for two hours
Put the butter on the fire and when it has taken color, add the Fontina, but of the milk in which it has been soaking, keep only two spoonfuls
Work it well with a wooden spoon without letting it boil and when the cheese is completely melted, remove it from the fire to add the yolks
Put it back on the fire for a little while, stirring again and in winter, pour it into a warm serving dish
If it has turned out well it should be neither grainy nor stringy, but have the appearance of a dense cream

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Caffè-latte Gelato (Iced Coffee and Milk)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Put the sugar in the milk and dissolve it over heat
Pour the mixture into the ice cream maker, as for ice creams in general
Serve it, when it will be solidified, in cups or small glasses

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cappelletti all'uso di Romagna (Cappelletti Romagna Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Ricotta, or half ricotta and half cacio raviggiolo, 180 grams
Half breast of capon cooked in butter, seasoned with salt and pepper, and finely minced with a crescent-shaped knife
Eggs, one whole and one yolk
Nutmeg flavor, few spices, lemon zest for those who like it
Flour for the pasta sheet, made with eggs only

steps: Taste the mixture so you can correct it if needed, as the ingredients do not always correspond in the same way. If capon breast is lacking, substitute with 100 grams of lean pork from the loin, cooked and seasoned in the same manner.
If the ricotta or raviggiolo are too soft, leave out the egg white or add another yolk if the mixture seems too firm.
To close them, make a rather tender pasta sheet of flour with eggs only, using also any remaining egg white, and cut it with a round disk the size of that shown on this page.
Place the mixture in the middle of the disks and fold them in two forming a half-moon; then take the two ends of the same, join them together and you will have the completed cappelletto.
If the pasta sheet dries out in your hand, dampen with a finger dipped in water the edges of the disks.
Cook the cappelletti in capon broth as is customary in Romagna.
A discreet eater is satisfied with two dozen.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cappone Arrosto Tartufato (Roasted Truffle-Stuffed Capon)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: One capon with only the breast, that is empty, without the neck and legs, killed the day before, weighing about 800 grams
Black or white truffles, fragrant, 250 grams

steps: Keep the truffles large as walnuts, lightly peel them and throw the skin thus raw inside the capon; you can also insert some slices of raw truffle under the skin.
Put the butter on the fire and when it is melted throw in the truffles with the Marsala, salt and pepper for seasoning and, on high heat, let them boil for only two minutes, stirring them constantly.
Removed from the pan, let them cool until the fat is set and then pour everything into the capon, sewing it both in the lower part and in the front where the neck was removed.
Keep it in a cool place to cook it after 24 hours, giving it thus three days of aging.
If it were a pheasant or a turkey, regulate yourself in proportion. In winter, it is good to keep them filled three or four days before cooking them, indeed for the pheasant you must wait.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cappone in Galantina (Capon in Galantine)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one large capon, plucked (approximately 1.5 kilograms), emptied and deboned (resulting in 0.7 kilograms)
Pork and veal for the forcemeat, 200 grams total
Breadcrumb marrow soaked in broth, 60 grams

steps: Cut the truffles into pieces the size of hazelnuts and blanch the pistachios in hot water to remove skins.
Cut the veal, pork, ham, and salted tongue into fillets the thickness of a finger and set aside after salting.
Make a forcemeat by pounding together 200 grams of pork and veal with 60 grams of breadcrumb marrow soaked in broth.
Add one egg, truffle skins, and scraps of tongue and ham to the forcemeat. Season with salt and pepper and pound until fine.
Pass the forcemeat through a sieve.
Lay out the deboned capon and salt it lightly.
Spread a thin layer of forcemeat on the capon, then arrange a layer of fillets interspersed with truffle pieces and pistachios.
Continue alternating layers of fillets and forcemeat, placing the young hen breast fillets toward the tail to avoid accumulating the same meat on the capon's breast.
Draw the sides of the capon together and sew it closed.
Tie it lengthwise with kitchen twine, wrap it tightly in a clean cloth, and tie both ends.
Boil in water for two and a half hours.
Remove from the cloth, rewrap it, and place it under a weight in a flat position for at least two hours to compress it into a flattened form.
The cooking water can be used for broth or gelatin.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cappone in Vescica (Capon in Bladder)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one large, thick bladder of beef or pork without defects
salt, 150 grams (plus a good handful for inside the capon)
prosciutto, 150 grams (sliced very thin, more lean than fat)
one wooden tube approximately one palm's length to serve as an air vent, shaped with a whistle-like mouth at top and a notch at bottom for tying

steps: Wash the bladder well in tepid water and soak it for one or two days.
Clean out the capon and remove the neck and legs.
Place a good handful of salt inside the capon, tuck in the leg joints, and fold the wings against the body so the tips do not pierce the bladder.
Sew closed the openings of the eviscerated cavity and neck.
Wrap the capon all over with 150 grams of thinly sliced prosciutto (more lean than fat), binding the slices tightly to the capon with twine.
Make a small incision in the bladder just large enough to fit the capon, then place the capon inside.
Sew the bladder closed.
Insert the wooden tube (with its whistle-mouth end on top and notched end at bottom) into the neck of the bladder and tie it in place.
Place the capon in a pot of tepid water and bring to a boil.
Boil gently for three continuous hours with the tube protruding, maintaining only small, sparse bubbles rising to the surface—this is the critical point.
If fat or other liquid comes from the tube, do not be concerned; collect it in a small pan.
Once cooked, let the capon cool in its water.
Serve the next day, discarding the prosciutto wrapper which will have lost its flavor.
Inside the capon you will find gelatin, and you may add additional gelatin as a garnish if desired.
Serves ten people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carciofi Fritti (Fried Artichokes)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cut 8 to 10 pieces per artichoke, even if not very large. As you cut them, throw them into fresh water and when they have refreshed well, remove them and dry them roughly or squeeze them only, throwing them immediately into flour so it adheres well.

Whisk the egg white to half stiff peaks, as one is enough for two artichokes, then into the white mix the yolk and salt it. Put the artichokes in a small sieve to shake off excess flour and then pass them through the egg, mix and let them sit a little so the egg incorporates. Throw the pieces one by one into a pan with boiling lard and when they have taken on a nice golden color remove them and serve at table with lemon wedges because, as everyone knows, acid on fried foods that are not sweet always adds grace and excitement to good drinking. If you desire that the artichokes remain white, it is better to fry them in oil and squeeze half a lemon in the water when you soak them.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carciofi in Gratella (Grilled Artichokes)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Choose tender artichokes, trim them, cut the stem at the base and leave them with all their leaves.
Open them out somewhat so they will take the seasoning well, which should be composed of nothing but oil, pepper and salt.
Place them upright on the grill, and if necessary to hold them firm, skewer them on a stick near the stem two or three together.
Give them another brushing of oil halfway through cooking and leave them on the fire until the outer leaves are burned.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carciofi in Salsa (Artichokes in Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the hard leaves from the artichokes, trim them, and peel the stems.
Divide them into four parts, or at most six if they are large.
Place them on the fire with butter in proportion and season with salt and pepper.
Shake the pan to turn them, and when they have drawn a good part of their moisture, wet them with broth to cook them completely.
Remove them dry, and in the remaining sauce add a pinch of chopped parsley, one or two teaspoons of finely ground breadcrumbs, lemon juice, more salt and pepper if needed.
Bring to a boil while stirring; then remove the sauce from the fire and when it stops boiling, add one or two egg yolks according to the quantity.
Return it briefly to the fire with more broth to make it liquid.
Add the artichokes to reheat them and serve them especially as a side dish for boiled meat.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carciofi in Umido colla Nepitella (Artichokes Braised with Catnip)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: tomato sauce or tomato paste dissolved in water

steps: Remove all inedible leaves from the artichokes and divide each into four wedges, or even six if they are large.
Flour them and place them on the fire in a copper pan with oil in proportion, seasoning with salt and pepper.
When you have browned them, add a small mixture composed of one clove of garlic, or half if the artichokes are few, and a good pinch of fresh nepitella.
When they have released their moisture, finish cooking them with tomato sauce or tomato paste dissolved in water.
They can serve as a side dish or be eaten alone.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carciofi Ripieni (Stuffed Artichokes)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: tender artichoke leaves from the center
prosciutto, more fat than lean, 50 grams
bread marrow from day-old bread, crumbled, a handful

steps: Cut the stem at the base, remove the small outer leaves, and wash the artichokes.

Trim them as the previous ones and open their inner leaves so that you can cut out with a small knife the central choke, and once removed the hair if there is any in the center, keep only the tender small leaves to add to the filling.

For six artichokes, compose the filling from the aforementioned small leaves, 50 grams of prosciutto more fat than lean, one quarter of a young onion, garlic the size of a nail tip, a few celery and parsley leaves, a pinch of softened dried mushrooms, a handful of bread marrow from day-old bread reduced to crumbles, and a pinch of pepper.
First chop the prosciutto with a knife, then everything together with the crescent-shaped tool, and with this mixture fill the artichokes which you will season and cook as the previous ones.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carciofi Ripieni di Carne (Artichokes Stuffed with Meat)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: prosciutto more fat than lean, 30 grams
one central choke from the artichokes

steps: For six artichokes, compose the filling as described.
When the artichokes have taken color with oil alone, pour a little water and cover them with a cloth dampened and held firm by the lid.
The steam that emanates, reaching them from all sides, cooks them better.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carciofi Ritti (Upright Artichokes)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove only the small and useless leaves near the stem, cutting the latter short.
Trim the top with a knife and spread apart the internal leaves somewhat.
Place them upright in a pan, together with the peeled and whole stems.
Season with salt, pepper, and oil, all in good measure.
Sauté them while keeping them covered, and when they are well browned, pour a little water into the pan and finish cooking them with the same.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carciofi Seccati per l'Inverno (Dried Artichokes for Winter)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Aromatic herbs (such as thyme, basil, celery leaves)

steps: Prepare them at the peak of harvest when they cost little; however, choose good quality artichokes at the right degree of maturity.
Remove all the tough leaves, trim the tips, clean a good length of the stem and cut them into four wedges, removing the fuzzy center if any.
As you cut them, throw them into fresh water acidulated with vinegar or lemon so they do not become black.

For the same reason, put them on the fire in an earthenware pot containing boiling water to which it is well to give flavor with a bundle of aromatic herbs, such as thyme, basil, celery leaves and similar.
Ten minutes of boiling, or even only five if they are tender, will be sufficient to cook them halfway.
Drain them and put them on a grating to dry in the sun; then string them and finish drying them in the shade in a ventilated place.
If possible do not keep them so long in the sun lest they acquire the smell of hay.
When used for frying or as a side dish to stewed dishes, soften them in boiling water.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cardoni con la Balsamella (Cardoons with Béchamel Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Discard the hardest ribs, clean the others from filaments and boil them until half cooked.

Cut the cardoon ribs into pieces about three fingers long and cook them to taste with butter and sufficient salt, finish cooking them by adding milk, or better cream, then bind them with a little béchamel sauce N. 137.
Add a pinch of grated Parmesan and remove them immediately without letting them boil again.
This is an excellent side dish to braised meats, bracioles, stewed giblets and other similar dishes.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cardoni in Gratella (Cardoons on the Grill)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: After boiling the cardoons, dry them well, leave the ribs about a palm long, season them generously with oil, pepper and salt and brown them on the grill.
They can serve as a side dish to steak or grilled fish.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cardoni in Teglia (Cardoons in a Pan)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: First remove the filaments from the cardoons carefully and give them half cooking in salted water, then throw them immediately into fresh water so they do not blacken.
Cut them into small pieces, flour them and when the oil begins to boil, throw them in and season with salt and pepper.
Beat the eggs first and wait to pour them when the cardoons are browned on both sides.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cardoni in Umido (Cardoons Stewed)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: After boiling them as in the preceding recipe, stew them with a mixture of garlic and parsley; oil, salt and pepper.
If you desire them more pleasing to the taste and of better appearance, cover them with an egg and lemon sauce when they are already on the serving dish.
Beat some eggs with lemon juice, put the liquid on the fire in a small pan stirring the spoon, and pour it when it begins to thicken.
If you do not use the sauce, season them at least with a pinch of Parmesan.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carne all'Imperatrice (Beef à l'Impératrice)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lean beef from the neck, 500 grams

steps: If you do not have a meat grinder to reduce to paste both the meat and the ham, use a knife and a mortar. Add the Parmesan and eggs, season the mixture with salt and pepper, mix it well, and with wet hands form it into a flattened patty two fingers high.

Place 30 grams of butter and two spoonfuls of oil on the fire in a baking dish or pot; when they begin to boil place the said flattened patty of meat on it and on the same sprinkle a clove of garlic cut into slices and some sprigs of rosemary. Let it boil, and when it begins to dry out wet it with tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water. Send it to table surrounded by its sauce.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carne alla genovese (Genoese-Style Veal)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: lean braciuola of veal weighing 300 to 400 grams

steps: Take a lean braciuola of veal weighing 300 to 400 grams, pound it and flatten it well.

Beat three or four eggs, season them with salt and pepper, a pinch of Parmesan, some chopped parsley and fry them in butter in the form of a frittata, approximately the width of the braciuola on which you will spread it, trimming where it overlaps and placing the trimmings where it is lacking.
After this, roll the braciuola together with the frittata tightly and tie it; then dust it with flour and place it in a pot with butter, seasoning it with salt and pepper.
When it has been well browned on all sides, moisten it with broth to finish cooking it and serve it with its own sauce, which because of the flour will be somewhat thick.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Carote Fritte (Fried Carrots)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Without peeling them, cut them into thin fillets the length of a finger
Salt them and after a few hours, taking them up still moist, pass them through flour and shake them free of it
Place them in egg, turn them in it, and taking the fillets one by one with your fingers, throw them into the pan
These carrots can serve as a side dish for a fry when there are no more zucchini

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Castagnole I (Fried Dough Balls)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: On a work surface, make a firm dough with flour, two eggs, a tablespoon of meat stock, lemon zest and salt to taste.
Work it thoroughly and strongly with your hands as you would common bread, making it gradually absorb a tablespoon of fine oil little by little.
Finally, shape it into small sticks, cut them into pieces the size of a walnut and immediately put them in a pan over low heat, stirring continuously.
When the castagnole are cooked, dust them with powdered sugar and serve them cold, as they are better cold than hot.
Note: if you use cognac or brandy instead of meat stock, you will not obtain the same effect and they will not puff up as much.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Castagnole II (Fried Dough Balls)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Put the egg yolks, sugar, meat stock, water and salt in a bowl.
Mix, beat the egg whites and with these ingredients and the butter knead enough flour on a work surface to form a dough that can be worked with your hands.
Work it thoroughly to refine it, then make small balls the size of a small walnut and fry them as the previous ones over low heat in plenty of fat.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cavallucci di Siena (Sienese Spiced Pastries)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Chop the walnuts to roughly the size of vetch.
Cut the candied orange into small cubes.

Place the sugar on the fire with one third of its weight in water and when reduced to thread stage, throw all the ingredients into it, stir and pour the hot mixture onto the work surface over the flour to knead it; you will need more flour to make the dough consistent.
Form the cavallucci, from which you will obtain over 40 with this amount, and since this dough sticks due to the sugar, dust them with flour on the surface.
Place them on a baking sheet and bake them in white at moderate heat.

Pay careful attention to the cooking of the sugar, because if it cooks too much it becomes dark. When, taking a drop between thumb and forefinger, it begins to form a thread, that is enough for this use.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cavolfiore all'uso di Romagna (Cauliflower Romagna Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one large head of cauliflower or two small ones

steps: Divide the cauliflower into small florets and wash them
Cook the raw, unwashed florets as follows: heat a chopped mixture of garlic, parsley and oil over the fire, and when it is browned, stop the cooking with a little water
Add the cauliflower, season with salt and pepper, and when it has absorbed the mixture, finish cooking it using tomato preserve dissolved in hot water
Add grace and more flavor with parmesan cheese when serving it at table, where it can serve as a side dish to boiled meat, a stew, or a coteghino

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cavolfiore Colla Balsamella (Cauliflower with Béchamel)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the leaves and green ribs from a large head of cauliflower, make a deep cross-cut in the stem and cook it in salted water.
Cut it into small florets and season to taste with butter, salt and pepper.
Place it in a fireproof dish, sprinkle a small pinch of Parmesan over it, cover it entirely with béchamel sauce and brown the surface.
Serve this cauliflower hot as a side dish or better accompanied by a meat stew or boiled chicken.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cavolo bianco per contorno (White Cabbage as a Side Dish)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Take a head of cabbage, cut it crosswise from the stem to form four parts and cut each of these into small pieces.
Keep it soaked in fresh water, and blanch it in salted water and, removed from the fire, drain it well without squeezing it.
Make a beaten mixture of ham and onion and put it on the fire with a piece of butter.
When the onion has taken on red color, stop it with a ladle of broth, boil a little and then pass the gravy.
In this gravy put back the cabbage with a piece of ham, season with pepper and little salt and boil it slowly to finish cooking it.
Remove the ham and send it to the table as a side dish to boiled meat.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cavolo nero per contorno (Black Cabbage as a Side Dish)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the hard ribs, boil it and mince it finely.

If you do not have meat gravy, make a small beaten mixture of ham and onion, put it on the fire with a piece of butter and when the onion is well browned, wet it with a drop of broth and pass the gravy formed.
In it throw the cabbage, season with pepper, little or no salt, add another piece of butter and more broth, if needed, and serve it as a side dish to boiled meat or coteghino.

Some use for a soup to roast slices of bread thick a finger, rub them with garlic, dip them barely in the water in which the black cabbage has boiled, placing the cabbage itself on it, still hot, and seasoning it with salt, pepper and oil. This, which is called in Florence cabbage with slices, is a dish for Carthusians or to be inflicted as penance on a glutton.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cavolo ripieno (Stuffed Cabbage)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: sugo dello stracotto (gravy from the braised meat)

steps: Take a large head of cabbage, clean it from the hard leaves on the surface, trim the stem evenly and give it half cooking in salted water.
Place it upside down to drain, then open the leaves one by one up to the center head and pour the filling on it.
Pull all the leaves back over it, close it completely and tie it in a cross pattern.
For the filling, make it with braised milk veal alone, or united with chicken livers and sweetbreads, everything minced finely.
To grace and make the mixture delicate, add a little béchamel, a pinch of Parmesan, an egg yolk and the flavor of nutmeg.
Finish cooking the cabbage in the gravy of the said braised meat, adding a piece of butter, with light fire below and above.
If you do not want to fill the whole cabbage, you can fill the wider leaves one by one by wrapping them over themselves like bobbins.
To the béchamel, a bread crumb soaked in broth or gravy can substitute.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cavolo Verzotto per Contorno (Glazed Cabbage as a Side)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Parboil it, squeeze out the water, chop it with a crescent-shaped blade, put it on the fire with butter and milk to cook it through and salt it.
When it is well cooked unite to it béchamel that is rather firm; make sure it incorporates well on the fire with the cabbage and add grated parmigiano.
Taste it to check if it has flavor and if the seasoning is right and serve it as a side with boiled meat or a meat stew.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cefali in gratella (Mullet Grilled)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the scales and gills from the fish but do not gut them as the entrails are the best part.
Season them with salt and pepper only and place them on the grill over a hot fire.
When cooked, place them between two hot plates away from the fire for five minutes.
At the moment of serving, turn the plates so the one on top goes underneath and the rendered fat remains spread over the fish.
Serve at table with lemon to squeeze over.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cenci (Tuscan Fried Pastries)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a fairly firm dough with these ingredients
Work it very thoroughly by hand and let it rest a little, floured and wrapped in a cloth
If it becomes too tender to work, add more flour
Roll out a sheet the thickness of a coin
Cut it with a knife or fluted wheel into strips about a palm long and two or three fingers wide
Make some cuts in these strips so you can fold, braid or crumple them before frying
Drop them into a pan where the fat, oil or lard, floats in abundance, in bizarre shapes
Dust with powdered sugar when they are no longer hot

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cialdoni (Waffle Rolls)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Place in a pot the flour, sugar, lard, and cold water.
Dissolve first, with the water, the flour and sugar, then add the lard.

Place the waffle iron over a hot burner and when it is well heated open it and pour over it each time half a tablespoon of the said batter; press the two parts of the iron together, pass it over the fire on one side and the other, remove the excess with a knife and open it when you know the waffle has taken a hazelnut color.

Then detach it somewhat from one side with the knife and immediately while still hot on the iron itself or on a cloth spread on the hearth roll it up with a reed bocciuolo or simply with your hands. This last operation must be done very quickly because if the waffle cools you will no longer be able to roll it up on itself.
If the waffles stick to the iron, oil it from time to time with lard, and if they do not all turn out well, add a bit of flour.
You already know that cialdoni can be served alone; but it is better to accompany them with cream or whipped cream and also with brûléed milk or Portuguese milk.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Ciambelle ossia Buccellati I (Ring Cakes I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in a bowl with half the milk, adding enough flour to make a bread of proper consistency
After forming it, let it sit surrounded by flour to a depth of more than a finger

Place the bowl in a warm place, protected from air, and when that bread is well risen (which will take eight to ten hours depending on the season), break it down and remake it larger with the rest of the milk and flour needed
Wait for it to rise again and be well puffed up (which will take about the same time), then pour it onto the work surface and knead it with the rest of the flour and all the ingredients mentioned
Work it very well and with force so that the dough refines and becomes completely homogeneous
Prepare iron baking sheets or tinned copper pans, greased with lard and floured, and in them place the ring cakes which you will make as large as you like, but so that they have plenty of room
Let them rise in the kitchen or in another place of warm temperature, and when they are well puffed up but not over-risen, make long incisions on the surface with the point of a knife
Brush them with egg and sprinkle coarsely crushed crystal sugar over them
Bake them in the oven at moderate heat

In winter it is advisable to knead the yeast with lukewarm milk and send the ring cakes to rise in a warm place. With half the dose you can obtain four beautiful ring cakes of about 350 grams each, if you do not want to make them smaller

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Ciambelle ossia Buccellati II (Ring Cakes II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lemon peel flavoring or anise or candied citron in small pieces

steps: Make a well in the flour to put the melted butter, eggs, and sugar in it
Mix the flour with these ingredients and with the milk needed to form a dough of proper consistency and work it well
Add the two powders and flavorings last
Instead of one ring cake you can make two and keep them with a wide hole, which come out quite thick
Make some incisions on the surface, brush them with egg yolk and bake them in the oven or country oven, greasing the pan with butter or lard
Also with half the doses you obtain a decent ring cake

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Ciambelline (Fried Pastry Rings)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Put in a saucepan 180 grams of water, a piece of butter the size of a large walnut, two teaspoons of sugar and a pinch of salt. When the liquid boils, dissolve 120 grams of flour in it, throwing it all at once so no lumps form and stir immediately with a spoon. Remove it quickly from the heat and while it is still boiling break one egg into it and mix strongly until it is well incorporated; then at intervals, when the mixture is cool, add two more eggs, working always and much with the spoon until it is well worked; and this is known by the action of the spoon itself, which, in the spaces it leaves, draws behind itself a thin veil of paste. Give it the scent of vanilla and prepare on a work surface a certain quantity of flour on which you will pour this paste. Then begin to work it with your hands covered in the same flour and roll it in so that it takes enough flour to become manageable, but still rather soft.

Divide this dough into 16 or 18 parts, forming as many little balls that will be a little more than walnut-sized: to each of these balls make a hole in the middle by pressing them with the tip of a finger against the work surface and turning them on themselves; flip them and do the same on the opposite side so the hole becomes large and graceful; thus these balls will take the form of little rings. Now put a wide-mouthed pot of water on the fire, and when the water is quite hot, but not boiling, throw the rings into it three or four at a time. If they stick to the bottom lift them slightly with a slotted spoon, turn them and when they come to the surface remove them dry and place them on a cloth, then with the tip of a knife make around and around each one, both on the outside and inside, an incision or even two at a certain distance, so they can puff better.

In this state you can leave them for hours if it suits you. Fry them with plenty of fat, lard or oil, over low heat, stirring the pan often; if they have come out well you will see them grow to an extraordinary volume, remaining dry. While still hot, but not boiling, dust them with powdered sugar and serve them.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Ciarlotta (Charlotte)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a cream with the milk, sugar, flour, egg and lemon zest
Make a syrup by boiling the sugar in water for ten minutes; when cooled squeeze a lemon into it
Take 300 grams of sponge cake and with it, cut into slices, with fruit preserves and the said cream, fill a well-worked pudding mold
Lastly pour the said syrup into it to soak the sponge cake or ladyfingers, and after several hours unmold it and serve it
This dose will be enough for eight people

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Ciarlotta di mele (Apple Charlotte)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Crumb of stale bread, as much as needed
Fresh butter of good quality, as much as needed

steps: Peel the apples, cut them into quarters, remove the seeds and the compartments that contain them and place them in fresh water where the lemon has been squeezed
Remove these quarters of apple dry and cut them crosswise into thin slices, which you will place on the fire in a saucepan without water and with the piece of cinnamon
When they begin to liquefy, add the sugar and stir, moving them often until they are cooked
Then remove the cinnamon and use it as follows
Melt the butter on the fire and when it boils, that is very hot, dip as many slices of bread crumb as needed, less than one centimetre thick, which you will have prepared before
With these cover the bottom of a smooth round mold and line the walls with them so that no empty spaces remain
Pour the preserve in the middle and cover it with the same slices of bread dipped in butter
Cook it

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cibreo (Chicken Giblets Fricassee)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the gall bladder from the livers, blanch the crests with boiling water, cut them in two or three pieces and cut the livers in half.
Put on the fire with butter in proportion, first the crests, then the livers and last the testicles and season with salt and pepper, then broth if needed to cook these things.
In a small pot, put one or two egg yolks with a teaspoon or half only of flour, lemon juice and boiling broth whisking so the egg does not curdle.
Pour this sauce over the giblets when they are cooked, let it boil for a while and add more broth, if necessary, to make it more liquid, and serve it.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cicale Fritte (Fried Mantis Shrimp)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Wash the mantis shrimp and boil them in a little water, covered with a cloth with a weight on top; 15 minutes of boiling should be sufficient.
Shell them after cooking and, exposing the flesh, cut it into two pieces.
Dust with flour, dip in beaten and salted egg, and fry it.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cicale in Umido (Stewed Mantis Shrimp)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Before cooking, keep the mantis shrimp in fresh water so they don't drain and instead swell.
Make a battuto with garlic, parsley and oil; once browned, place the whole mantis shrimp in it and season with salt and pepper.
When they have taken on the seasoning, wet them with tomato juice or conserve and serve them on slices of bread dried over the fire.
Before bringing them to the table, make an incision with scissors along the back so they can be peeled more easily.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cicale Ripiene (Stuffed Mantis Shrimp)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Split the mantis shrimp along the back.
Fill it with a mixture of breadcrumbs, parsley and garlic scent.
Season both the filling and the fish with oil, pepper and salt.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cieche alla Pisana (Transparent Gobies Pisan Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Wash the gobies several times until they no longer produce foam.
Drain them on a sieve.
Heat oil with garlic cloves (slightly crushed) and sage leaves.
When the garlic is colored, add the gobies.
If still alive, cover with a lid so they do not jump away.
Season with salt and pepper, stir often with a spoon and moisten with a little water if they dry out too much.
When cooked, bind them with beaten eggs mixed separately with Parmesan, breadcrumbs, and lemon.
If serving in the cooking vessel, place between two fires at the end so they form a white crust on the surface.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cieche Fritte I (Fried Transparent Gobies I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the gobies in oil with whole garlic and sage as described in the Cieche alla Pisana recipe.
Remove the garlic and finely chop the gobies.
Beat eggs in proportion, salt them, add Parmesan and a little breadcrumbs.
Mix the gobies into the egg mixture.
Fry by spoonfuls to make small fritters.
Serve with lemon wedges.
Few will notice it is a fish dish when eaten this way.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cieche Fritte II (Fried Transparent Gobies II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Flour the gobies only with wheat flour or corn flour.
Fry in a pan.
This method makes them simpler but less good than the previous preparation.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cignale dolce-forte (Sweet and Sour Wild Boar)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Wild boar piece, approximately one kilogram, with skin and one finger-width of fat
Carrot, half of a large one
Celery, two white ribs, one palm-length

steps: Make a battuto with half an onion, half of a large carrot, two white celery ribs about one palm-length, a pinch of parsley, and 30 grams of prosciutto (both fat and lean).
Mince finely with a crescent knife (lunetta) and place in a pot with oil, salt, and pepper under the boar to cook together.
Brown the meat on all sides.
Drain off most of the fat and continue as directed in the recipe (the text is cut off at this point).

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cignale in Dolce-Forte (Wild Boar in Sweet-Strong Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: wild boar, about 1 kilogram with skin and a finger's width of fat
two stalks of white celery about a palm's length
30 grams of fatty and lean prosciutto
20 grams candied fruit in small pieces

steps: Make a battuto (finely chopped mixture) with half an onion, half a large carrot, two stalks of white celery about a palm's length, a pinch of parsley and 30 grams of fatty and lean prosciutto. Mince it finely with a crescent-shaped knife and place it in a pot with oil, salt and pepper under the wild boar to cook together.
When the piece has browned on all sides, drain most of the fat, sprinkle a pinch of flour over it, and finish cooking it with hot water poured in from time to time.

Meanwhile prepare the sweet-strong sauce in a glass with the following ingredients and add it to the pot after straining the cooking liquid: 40 grams raisins, 30 grams chocolate, 30 grams pine nuts, 20 grams candied fruit in small pieces, 50 grams sugar, and vinegar as needed (use sparingly as you can add more later).
Before serving, let it boil again so that the sauce incorporates well. Note that the sweet-strong sauce works better if made a day in advance.
If you prefer a simpler version, make the sweet-strong sauce with only sugar and vinegar.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Ciliege Visciole in Guazzo (Sour Cherries Preserved in Syrup)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: From the sour cherries, separate 200 grams of the worst or damaged ones, extract their juice and strain it
The others, having removed the stem, layer them in a crystal vase: one of cherries and one of sugar, then pour the said juice over them
Remove the pits from some of the damaged cherries and throw these along with the cinnamon into the vase
Close the vase and do not move it for at least two months
You will see that the sugar will gradually dissolve and the cherries will first float in the liquid, then as this converts to alcohol the cherries sink to the bottom and then they are edible and good

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cioccolata (Hot Chocolate)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 60 grams of chocolate for an abundant cup, or 50 grams if light is preferred, up to 80 grams if very thick is desired

steps: Break the chocolate into pieces and place in a chocolate pot with the water mentioned above
When it begins to be hot, stir it so that it does not stick and dissolves well
As soon as it comes to a boil, remove it from the fire and whisk it for five minutes
Then bring it to a boil again and serve it

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cipolline Agro-Dolci (Sweet and Sour Pearl Onions)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Choose small white onions, about the size of a walnut
Peel them and trim away any excess
Blanch them in salted boiling water
In a saucepan, heat the sugar over dry heat until liquefied
Add the flour and stir continuously with a wooden spoon
When the mixture turns red, gradually add two-thirds glass of water mixed with vinegar
Let the liquid boil until any lumps dissolve
Add the pearl onions and shake the saucepan frequently, being careful not to touch them with a spoon to avoid damaging them
Taste before serving and adjust sugar or vinegar if needed

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cipolline in Istufa (Braised Pearl Onions)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Peel the onions and trim the top and bottom evenly
Boil them in salted water for ten minutes
Brown a piece of butter until it turns hazelnut color
Add the onions, season with salt and pepper, and brown on one side
Turn them over and brown on the other side
Wet them with meat stock and bind with flour mixed with butter

Alternatively, if meat stock is unavailable, cook them in white: after boiling and cooling in fresh water, place them in a saucepan with a mirepoix bundle, a small slice of prosciutto, a piece of butter, and a ladle of broth
Season with pepper and little salt
Cover with very thin slices of lard and place a sheet of butter-greased paper on top
Finish cooking between two fires and serve as a side dish with the reduced sauce

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cipolline per Contorno ai Coteghini (Pearl Onions as a Side to Cotechino Sausage)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Broth from cotechino sausage, half a ladle

steps: Boil the onions as described in the previous recipe
Sauté them in butter and season with salt and pepper
Wet them with defatted broth from the cotechino sausage
Add vinegar and sugar to enhance them

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Claret Cup (English Beverage)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Red wine of excellent quality, 5 decilitres

steps: Boil the sugar in the water for five minutes.
Removed from the fire, squeeze the lemons into this syrup and pour in the wine, then strain it through a cloth.
Return it to the fire to boil slowly for 25 minutes and when it is cold bottle it.
Use it diluted with water and chilled with ice in summer.
If you need to keep it for a long time, keep it in the cellar.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Composta di Cotogne (Quince Compote)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Water, one and a half glasses

steps: Peel the quinces and cut them into wedges not too large, removing the middle part that was part of the core
Place them on the fire with water and when they have boiled covered for a quarter of an hour, pour in the fine sugar
Once cooked, remove them dry and place them in the dish you want to serve at the table; reduce the remaining juice to make it into a syrup, then pour it over the quinces and serve them cold

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conchiglie Ripiene (Stuffed Shells)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a béchamel sauce with the milk, butter and flour
When removing it from the fire, add the Parmesan and, no longer at boiling point, the egg yolks and the minced fish, seasoning with salt and pepper
Pour it into shells buttered beforehand with cold butter
Brown it slightly in a country oven and serve it
Alternatively, the shells could be filled with minced cooked chicken flesh keeping the same proportions

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Coniglio Arrosto (Roasted Rabbit)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Stud it with lardons.
Baste with oil or, better, with butter and salt when cooking is almost complete.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva di Albicocche (Apricot Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: White fine sugar in powder, 800 grams per kilogram of apricots

steps: Take well-ripened apricots of good quality, as it is an error to believe that with inferior fruit one can obtain the same effect.
Remove the pit and put them on the fire without water, and while they boil, break them down with a spoon to reduce them to a pulp.
When they have boiled for about half an hour, pass them through a strainer to clean them of skins and filaments.
Then return them to the fire with white fine sugar in powder in the proportion of eight tenths, that is 800 grams of sugar for every kilogram of apricots passed.
Stir them often with a spoon until they reach the consistency of preserve, which is known by pouring a spoonful from time to time onto a plate, on which it should run slowly.
Pour it hot into jars and when it is cold cover it with oiled butcher's paper adhering to the preserve, and seal the mouth of the jar with thick paper tied with twine around it.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva di Aranci (Orange Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Fine white sugar, equal to the weight of the oranges
Water, half the weight of the oranges

steps: With the prongs of a fork prick the entire skin of the oranges.
Keep them soaked for three days, changing the water morning and evening.
On the fourth day cut them in half and each half into strips about half a centimeter thick, discarding the seeds.
Weigh them and only then regulate the sugar and water according to the proportions indicated.
Put them on the heat first with water alone and after ten minutes of boiling add the lemon cut like the oranges.
Immediately after add the sugar and stir continuously until the liquid resumes a strong boil, because otherwise the sugar precipitates to the bottom and could stick to the pan.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva di Aranci Forti (Bitter Orange Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Sugar, 150 grams per 100 grams of fruit (white, fine)

steps: Boil the bitter oranges in water until they can be easily passed through from one side to the other with a stick.
Remove them from the boiling water and place them in cold water and keep them there for two days, changing the water often.
Cut them as the previous recipe, cleaning them of seeds and those white filaments found inside.
After weighing them, put them on the fire without water with 150 grams of white fine sugar for every 100 grams of fruit.
Boil slowly and be careful that the syrup does not condense too much, otherwise the oranges will harden.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva di Azzeruole (Medlar Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Throw the azzeruoles into boiling water with their stems attached.
Boil for ten minutes.
While still hot, with the point of a small knife remove the pits from the flower end.
If any lose their shape, reshape with your fingers.
Peel them without removing the stem.
Dissolve the sugar in the 7 deciliters of water (which can be the water in which they boiled).
Add the azzeruoles and when the syrup taken with a spoon begins to fall in drops, remove them with their liquid and preserve in jars.
They remain like candied fruit and are very good.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva di Lampone (Raspberry Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: White powdered sugar, equal weight to the strained raspberries

steps: Put the raspberries on the heat as they are without fermentation.
Boil for about twenty minutes.
Pass through a sieve.
Weigh the strained raspberries.
Return to the heat with an equal amount of white powdered sugar.
Boil until it reaches the consistency of preserve, which you will know by the methods already indicated.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva di More (Blackberry Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Crush the blackberries by hand.
Bring to boil for about ten minutes.
Pass through a sieve.
Return to the heat with the mentioned sugar to reduce to the consistency of fruit preserves.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva di Pomodoro Senza Sale (Tomato Preserve Without Salt)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Choose field tomatoes rather than garden tomatoes, as they are less watery, and prefer small ones to large ones.
Crush them roughly and put them in a copper pot (not tinned) over a wood fire. Do not worry about the acid attacking the copper when it is on the fire and retains the heat of boiling.

When they are cooked and broken down, pour them into a tightly-woven sack held suspended and, once the water has drained, pass them through a strainer to clean them of seeds and skins, squeezing them well.

Wash the pot carefully and return them to the fire to reduce them as needed. To know the precise point of consistency the preserve should have, pour a few drops onto a plate and if you see that it does not run and does not present watery seroseness around it, that will mean this is the correct point of cooking.
Then bottle it, and you will have another proof of its sufficient density if you see it descend with difficulty through the funnel.

Prefer small bottles to consume them quickly; they can remain unopened for 12 or 13 days without the preserve suffering. Use white bottles that come in commerce with Recoaro water, or in their absence, half-bottles of dark beer. Seal them with cork stoppers put on by hand, but which seal well, and tie them with twine, taking care to leave a little air between the stopper and the liquid.

Place the said bottles in a pot amongst hay, rags, or similar things so that they stand tightly together, and pour into the pot enough water that reaches up to the neck of the bottles and heat from underneath. Watch as soon the stopper of the bottles will show signs of rising and spraying away if it were not tied, and then stop the fire, because the operation is truly finished.
Remove the bottles when the water is cold or even before, replace with a finger the displaced stoppers to put them back in place and keep the bottles in the cellar.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva di Rose (Rose Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Place the roses in a bowl with 200 grams of the sugar and the juice of half a lemon and with your hands rub them, chop them as much as possible to reduce them to nearly a paste.

Dissolve the rest of the sugar in the water over the fire and add the roses to it to boil until the syrup is condensed, which is known if, taking a drop between the fingers, it begins to stick; but be careful that it does not reach the thread stage.
Before removing them from the fire, give them color with breton, which you can omit if you do not care about the beautiful color.
When the preserve is cooled, put it in small jars to preserve it like all the other similar ones.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva di Susine (Plum Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Plums, preferably Claudia variety, any quantity
White powdered sugar, 60 grams per 100 grams of fresh plums

steps: Remove the pits from the plums.
Boil for a few minutes.
Pass through a sieve.
