Return to the heat with white powdered sugar in the proportion of 60 grams of sugar per 100 grams of fresh plums.
If mold forms after some time, it indicates insufficient cooking; remedy by returning to the heat.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva Dolce di Pomodoro (Sweet Tomato Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: The tomatoes for this use must be very ripe, pulpy, and possibly round.
Place them in very hot water so they can be peeled easily. After peeling, cut them in half and with the handle of a teaspoon remove the seeds.
Dissolve the sugar in the fire in two fingers (of a glass) of water, then throw in the tomatoes, the juice of the lemon, and a little of its grated skin.
During boiling over low heat in an uncovered pan, stir somewhat, and if any seeds appear that have remained, remove them.
Finally give it flavor with vanillated sugar and remove it when it has reached the consistency of common preserves.
Note: It is difficult to specify the quantity of sugar in this preserve, as it depends on how watery the tomatoes are. Make double the dose as it reduces greatly.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva Liquida di Cotogne (Liquid Quince Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: White powdered sugar, equal to the weight of the raw quinces

steps: Cut the quinces into segments.
Remove the hard part of the core.
Leave the skin on and after weighing them, put them on the heat covered with water.
When well cooked, pass them and return them to the heat with the water in which they boiled and as much white powdered sugar as was their raw weight, waiting to pour it when they are boiling.
Stir often and when (pouring a few drops on a plate) you do not see it running too much, remove it.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Conserva Soda di Cotogne (Firm Quince Preserve)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Quinces, cleaned of skin and core, 800 grams
Water, half a glass and one glass

steps: Dissolve the sugar on the heat with half a glass of water.
Boil it a little and set it aside.
Cut the quinces into very thin slices.
Put them on the heat with one glass of water in a copper pan.
Keep them covered but stir often, trying to chop and crush them with a spoon.
When they become tender from cooking, add the prepared sugar syrup.
Stir often and let boil uncovered until the preserve is done, which you will know when it begins to fall in shreds taken up on a spoon.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Contorno di Filetti di Sogliole a un Fritto dello Stesso Pesce (Side Dish of Sole Fillets with a Fried Sole Preparation)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: sole fish, a pair of medium size or one large

steps: Take a pair of medium sole or one large sole, remove the fillets after skinning them (there will be four), and cut them crosswise into fine strips like matches
If you cut them at an angle they will be somewhat longer and better
Put them in a bowl with the juice of one or more lemons as needed and let them marinate for two or three hours, which will make them firm, otherwise they would be limp
Shortly before serving, dry them with a cloth, immerse in milk, flour them, make sure they don't clump, and fry in oil
Salt them lightly

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Coratella d'Agnello alla Bolognese (Lamb Offal, Bolognese Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: tomato juice or tomato paste dissolved in water or broth

steps: Cut the liver into thin slices and the lungs into pieces and throw them as is into a pan with lard.
When the offal is almost cooked, drain it from all the fat and add a piece of butter; continue frying.
Shortly after, pour tomato juice or tomato paste dissolved in water or broth into the pan.
Season with salt and pepper, serve it with this sauce, and be sure it will be praised.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cosciotto di Castrato Arrosto (Roasted Leg of Mutton)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Let it age for several days before cooking, more or less depending on temperature.
Beat it well with a wooden mallet before threading onto the spit.
Skin it and remove the middle bone without damaging it too much.
Tie it so it stays compact and apply intense heat at first, then reduce heat halfway through cooking.
When it begins to release juices, collect them in the dripping pan and baste with the same juices and degreased broth, nothing else.
Salt when cooking is almost complete; ensure it is not overcooked nor bloody.
Serve at table with its juices in a sauceboat and wrap the end of the leg bone in fringed white paper for better presentation.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cosciotto o Spalla di Castrato in Cazzaruola I (Braised Mutton Leg or Shoulder I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 1 kg shoulder or leg of mutton, boned
Strips of lardoon or prosciutto rind
1 bunch tied together of parsley, celery and carrot
Broken bones from the shoulder or leg
1 glass of broth or half a glass
Cold water to nearly cover the meat

steps: Bone the shoulder and lard it with lardoon strips
Season inside and out with salt and pepper
Roll it up and tie it to achieve a nice shape
Place it in a braising pan with 40 grams of butter to brown it
Add the lardoon or prosciutto rinds, the tied bunch of herbs, the whole onion, the broken bones, meat scraps if you have them, the glass of broth or half a glass, and 2 or 3 tablespoons of brandy
Add enough cold water so the liquid reaches just below the surface of the mutton
Cover the pan well and simmer slowly until the meat is cooked, which will take four or more hours if the animal is tough
Strain the sauce, degrease it and discard the excess
Serve the mutton, optionally garnished with carrots, turnips, or beans prepared according to the instructions given in the text

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cosciotto o Spalla di Castrato in Cazzaruola II (Braised Mutton Leg or Shoulder II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lardoon strips wrapped in salt and pepper
1 glass of water or better broth
Tomatoes, if in season, broken into pieces

steps: Bone the shoulder and lard it with lardoon strips wrapped in salt and pepper
Salt it somewhat
Roll it up and tie it tightly
Place it on the fire with 40 grams of butter and the half onion studded with a clove to take on color
Remove the braising pan from the fire and pour in a glass of water or better broth, 1 tablespoon of brandy, an aromatic bunch, and if it is tomato season, some tomatoes broken up
Boil gently for about three hours with the pan covered with double sheets of paper, turning the meat frequently
When cooked, discard the onion, strain the sauce, degrease it and add it to the meat when serving
Do not cook it too much or it will not be able to be cut into slices

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Costolette d'Agnello Vestite (Dressed Lamb Chops)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Truffle or softened and chopped dried mushrooms

steps: Take fine lamb chops, denude the bone of the chop, flatten them, trim them, cook them naturally in butter sautéed, season them hot with salt and pepper and set them aside.

Make a thick béchamel and in it throw prosciutto and salted tongue into very small dice, a pinch of Parmesan, a pinch of nutmeg and a truffle sliced or softened and chopped dried mushrooms, and set this mixture aside so it cools well.

Make a puff pastry proportioned to the quantity of chops and with it wrap them one by one, leaving the bone of the chop exposed, but first spread them abundantly on one side and the other with the said mixture.
When you have closed them, gild them with egg yolk, place them upright around the edge of a baking dish, cook them in a country oven and serve them hot.

You can cut the puff pastry with a paper template, so the wrapping will be more precise; for more neatness and elegance, before sending them to the table, wrap the end of each chop with scalloped white paper.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Costolette di Daino alla Cacciatora (Venison Chops Hunter-Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: venison chops from the loin, sliced thin

steps: Heat oil and butter in proportion to the quantity you have to cook, add one whole clove of garlic and several sage leaves.
When the garlic has browned, place the chops on top, season with salt and pepper and cook them quickly over high heat, basting them with marsala wine.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Costolette di Vitella di Latte alla Milanese (Milanese-Style Milk Veal Cutlets)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: After baring the bone of the cutlet and discarding the trimmings, flatten them with the blade of a large knife to widen and thin them.
Then make a mixture with prosciutto more fat than lean, a little parsley, grated Parmesan cheese, the aroma of truffles if you have them, and a little salt and pepper.
Spread this mixture on the cutlets on one side only, dip them in egg, then bread them and cook them sauté in butter, serving them with lemon wedges.
For five cutlets, if they are not very large, 50 grams of prosciutto and two heaping tablespoons of Parmesan will suffice.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Costolette nella Carta (Chops in Paper)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Take milk veal chops, denude the bone of the chop by removing the meat, cook them in butter sautéed and season them with salt and pepper.

Make a proportioned mixture of fat and lean prosciutto and parsley, chop it fine, add butter and breadcrumb marrow to hold it together and with this spread the chops on both sides, then decorate them with slices of raw truffles.
Cut thick white paper to the pattern of as many chops as there are, oil it with butter or oil on both sides and with it wrap them tightly with the bone of the chop outside.
Now place them on a grill on light fire, being careful that the paper does not burn and send them to the table, for more neatness, with the end of the chop wrapped in scalloped white paper.
Lamb chops can also be used for this purpose if they are large.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Coteghino Fasciato (Wrapped Coteghino)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Coteghino weighing about 300 grams, skinned raw
Lean veal or beef slice, 200 to 300 grams, wide and thin

steps: Skin the coteghino raw and beat the veal or beef slice well
Wrap the coteghino with the meat slice, tie it all with string and put it on the fire in a pot with a piece of butter, celery, carrot and a quarter onion, all cut coarsely
When the piece has taken color on all sides, pour in enough water to cover it halfway and add some pieces of dried mushrooms, letting it boil slowly until completely cooked
Pass the gravy, unite the mushrooms to it and use this with cheese and butter to dress pasta, serving the wrapped coteghino, freed from the string, with some of its gravy around it as accompaniment
To thicken the gravy for the pasta, put a pinch of flour in a pot with a piece of butter and when it begins to take color pour the gravy into it and let it boil a little
The contorno of carrots works well with this dish, first boiled to two-thirds done, then finished in that gravy

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cotognata (Quince Paste)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Put the quinces on the fire covered with water and when they begin to crack, remove them, peel them and scrape them as best you can to remove all the pulp, then pass it through a sieve.
Put it back on the fire with the sugar and stir it constantly so it doesn't stick.
Seven or eight minutes of boiling will be enough; but then, if taken up with a spoon it begins to fall in shreds, remove it.

If you put it in vessels it can serve you as a preserve and made this way it will remain whiter than the one I will describe at No. 741, but with less fragrance, because part of the particular odor of this fruit is lost in the water.
To reduce it to quince paste, spread it on a board about the thickness of a coin and dry it in the sun covered with a veil because flies and wasps are very fond of it.
When it is dry on top, cut it in the form of chocolate tablets and by passing a knife under it to detach it from the board, turn it over on the opposite side.

If you would like to give it bizarre forms, procure some tin molds empty on both sides, fill them, smooth them and detaching the marmalade from the edges carefully, place it equally on the board and dry it in the same manner.

You can also coat it with sugar if you wish, and then put 100 grams of white sugar to melt with two spoonfuls of water and when it has boiled enough to form a thread (taking a drop between two fingers) spread each piece with a brush.
If the sugar hardens during the operation (which is best to do on a not humid day) put it back on the fire with another drop of water and boil it again.
When the sugar is dry on one side and on the edges, spread the opposite side.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cotolette col Prosciutto (Veal Cutlets with Prosciutto)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Prosciutto, a very thin slice fat and lean
Parmesan or gruyere cheese, sliced very thin

steps: Prepare the cutlets as in the previous recipe and place them in the egg with a very thin slice of prosciutto fat and lean the size of the cutlet itself.
Coat them with the prosciutto stuck on top, salt lightly and brown them in butter on the side without the prosciutto.
Over the prosciutto, instead of truffles, spread very thin slices of parmesan or gruyere.
Finish cooking them with heat on top and serve with meat juice and lemon juice, or with tomato juice.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cotolette di Baccalà (Salt Cod Cutlets)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: bread crumb paste (made from bread marrow, water, and butter), 3-4 spoonfuls
lemon, cut into wedges or tomato sauce

steps: Boil the salt cod as in the preceding recipe.
Finely chop the anchovies, parsley, and salt cod together with a knife.
Add pepper, grated Parmesan, and the bread crumb paste made from bread marrow, water, and butter to make it more tender, along with two eggs.
Form the mixture into spoonfuls and dip each into breadcrumbs.
Flatten with your hands to give them the shape of cutlets.
Dip the cutlets into beaten egg and then coat again in breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil and serve with lemon wedges or tomato sauce.
Half this quantity will make 9 or 10 cutlets.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cotolette di Carciofi (Artichoke Cutlets)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Take two large artichokes, clean them of hard leaves and scrape the stem, then boil them, but not too much, and while still boiling cut them lengthwise into five slices each, leaving some stem, and season with salt and pepper.
Make a béchamel sauce: melt the butter, add the flour, and gradually add the milk, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and mix in an egg yolk, the Parmesan, and a pinch of salt.

Taking them up one by one by the stem, dip the artichoke slices in the béchamel, lay them on a tray and cover them with the remaining béchamel using a spoon. After several hours, when they are completely cold, coat them with a beaten egg, bread them, and fry them in oil or lard.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cotolette di Vitella di Latte coi Tartufi alla Bolognese (Milk-Fed Veal Cutlets with Truffles Bolognese Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Veal cutlet from the sotto-noce or lean parts of the thigh
Parmesan or gruyere cheese, sliced thin

steps: Cut the meat thin and the size of a palm of your hand. Beat them and give them a smooth and elegant shape, like a heart for example, wide at the top and narrowing at the bottom.
Prepare them on a plate with lemon juice, pepper, salt and very little grated parmesan.
Leave them in this infusion for an hour or two.
Pass them in beaten egg and keep them in it for the same amount of time.
Coat them with fine breadcrumbs and fry them with butter in a copper pan.
When they are just browned on one side, turn them and on the cooked side spread first slices of truffles and over these slices of parmesan or gruyere, cutting both as thin as possible.
Finish cooking them with heat under and over, adding broth or meat juice.
Remove them and arrange them on a platter with their juice around, squeezing the juice of a lemon over them, or half a lemon if there are few.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cotolette di Vitella di Latte in Salsa d'Uovo (Milk-Fed Veal Cutlets in Egg Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Brown and cook the cutlets sauté style as in recipes 312 and 313.
Spread over them a sauce of egg yolks, butter and lemon juice.
Keep them a little longer on the fire and serve.
For seven or eight cutlets, three egg yolks, 30 grams of butter and half a lemon, beaten together in a small pan before pouring, will suffice.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cotolette Imbottite (Stuffed Cutlets)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 170 grams veal or chicken or turkey breast, trimmed of bone

steps: Lightly fry the thin cutlets in butter, salt them, and set aside.
Make a béchamel sauce with the flour, butter, and milk. Once removed from heat, salt it, add the parmesan cheese and egg yolk, mixing well.
Once the béchamel has cooled, spread it on both sides of the cutlets to the thickness of a coin, evening it out with a knife blade dipped in oil.
Dip the cutlets in beaten egg, coat with breadcrumbs, and fry them in oil or lard until golden.
Serve with lemon wedges.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crema (Custard)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: First work the egg yolks with the sugar and then pour in the milk little by little
To speed up the cooking you can put the mixture on high heat, but as soon as you see it smoke reduce the heat so it does not curdle
If this happens, pass the cream through a sieve
Cooking is complete when the cream sticks to the spoon, which should be moved continuously around
Add the flavoring just before removing it from the fire

This cream, without flour or starch, in the proportions given, is excellent for cream ice cream. It can also be used for a liquid English trifle by adding, when cooled, slices of sponge cake or ladyfingers lightly moistened with rosolio; but if you wish to make it even more pleasing, add very thinly cut pieces of candied fruit

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crema alla Francese (French Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Eggs, one whole egg and 4 egg yolks

steps: Mix the sugar well together with the eggs, add the milk little by little and lastly the isinglass in its natural form.
Place the saucepan on the fire, stirring the spoon continuously always in one direction and when the cream begins to condense, sticking to the spoon, remove it.
Take a smooth mold with a hole in the middle, such that the quantity of cream can fill it, grease it with butter or with liqueur, so that a thin layer remains at the bottom and pour it into the same.
In summer place the mold in ice and in winter in fresh water and unmold it onto a folded towel on the platter.
If you do not trust the milk too much, give it a boil of at least a quarter of an hour before making the cream, or increase one sheet of isinglass.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crema Fritta I (Fried Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Work the eggs with the sugar, then add the cornstarch reduced to powder, the grated lemon zest, the milk poured little by little and the butter.

Put the mixture on the fire stirring continuously as you would for a common cream and when it is condensed so that it no longer grows, add the pinch of salt and pour it onto a tray or board, spreading it to the thickness of a finger.
Cut it into almond shapes when it is well cold, coat it with egg and breadcrumbs, fry it in lard or oil and serve it hot as a side dish to other fried foods.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crema Fritta II (Fried Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Keep it on the fire until the flour has lost its raw taste.
For the rest, proceed as with the previous recipe number.
Half the amount, mixed with other fried foods, will be enough for four or five people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crema Montata (Whipped Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Isinglass, 15 grams, equal to 6 or 7 sheets
Water, three quarters of a tablespoon glass
Flavoring, three whole cherry laurel leaves or other as you prefer

steps: Beat in a saucepan the egg yolks and the sugar, add the water and the said leaves and place it on the fire stirring the spoon, until it is cooked, which thing, as I have already told you, is known by its condensing and sticking to the spoon.
Then pour it into a basin and thus hot beat it firmly with a whisk until it has mounted; remove the leaves and continuing always to beat it, add, when it is mounted, the isinglass little by little.

Take a decorated mold, grease it with oil, surround it with ice and pour the whipped cream into it, in the middle of which, if you wish, you can put ladyfingers dipped in liqueur or smeared with fruit preserve.
Leave it in the ice for more than an hour, and if it does not want to unmold naturally, pass a cloth soaked in hot water around the mold.

The isinglass is prepared beforehand thus: it is first put in soak, then on the fire with two fingers of a glass of water, it is boiled until the water, evaporating in part, forms a somewhat dense liquid, which sticks between the fingers, and thus boiling is poured into the cream to which you can give the taste of alkermes, coffee or chocolate.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crescente (Bolognese Fried Flatbread)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Mix flour with cold water and salt, adding a little lard
Work and knead the dough
Heat lard in a pan until it boils and remove from fire
Drop the dough into the hot lard to fry
The flatbread will puff up better this way

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cresentine (Garlic-Rubbed Toasted Bread)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Toast bread slices on both sides.
While hot, rub them with a garlic clove.
Season with salt, oil, vinegar, and sugar.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Croccante (Almond Brittle)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: butter or oil for the mold

steps: Shell the almonds and separate the lobes, which are the two parts naturally joined together
Cut each lobe into thin strips, either lengthwise or crosswise as you prefer
Heat the cut almonds over the fire and dry them until they take on a yellowish color, without roasting them
Meanwhile, place the sugar in a pot, preferably not tinned, and heat until it is perfectly liquefied
When the sugar is liquid, pour the well-heated almonds into it and stir
To prevent the brittle from becoming bitter from overcooking, throw a shovel of ash onto the coals
The exact point of doneness is known by the cinnamon color the brittle acquires
Then pour it gradually into a mold previously greased with butter or oil, pressing it with a lemon against the walls and spreading it as thin as you can
Unmold while cold; if this proves difficult, immerse the mold in boiling water
Alternatively, you may dry the almonds in the sun, grind them finely with a crescent-shaped tool, and add a piece of butter when they are in the sugar

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Croccante a Bagno-Maria (Almond Brittle Custard)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Blanch the almonds and with a small curved knife reduce them to the size of grains of wheat approximately.
Put 110 grams of the said sugar on the fire and when it is completely melted, pour in the almonds and stir them continuously with a spoon until they have taken on a cinnamon color.
Throw them then into a pan greased with butter and, when they are cold, pound them in a mortar with the remaining 40 grams of sugar and reduce them very fine.
Add the egg yolks and then the milk, mix well and pour the mixture into a mold with a hole in the middle, which you will have first greased with butter.
Cook it in a water bath and after, if in summer, keep the mold in ice.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crocchette di Animelle (Croquettes of Sweetbreads)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: optional: fat and lean ham, salted tongue, truffles

steps: Take 150 grams of sweetbreads and cook them in gravy or with a small mixture of onion and butter
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg
Cut them into small dice and mix with two tablespoons of rather firm béchamel, adding one egg yolk and a good pinch of parmesan
Take the mixture up with small spoons and pour it into breadcrumbs, shaping it into an oblong form like a spool
Dip them in beaten egg, then coat again in breadcrumbs and fry them
You can make them more tasty if you add fat and lean ham, salted tongue cut into small dice to the mixture, and if instead of nutmeg you flavor them with small pieces of truffles
With the stated quantity of sweetbreads you will get ten or twelve croquettes which you can add to other types of fried foods to make a mixed fry dish

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crocchette di Patate (Potato Croquettes)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Peel the potatoes and if they are large cut them into four parts and put them to boil in salted water.
Pass them through a sieve while still hot and dry.
To the puree add the butter, melted if it is winter, and all the rest, mixing well.
Let the mixture cool well, divide it into ten or twelve parts and, over a light layer of flour, give them the shape of spools to obtain the croquettes.
Beat an egg and dip them one by one into it, coat them with breadcrumbs and fry them in oil or lard to serve as a side dish to fried meat or a roast.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crocchette di Riso Composte (Composed Rice Croquettes)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: rice croquette mixture (recipe from preceding recipe)
chicken giblets cooked in butter and gravy
or onion mixture if gravy is lacking

steps: Use the recipe for simple rice croquettes and mix into the rice when cooked and measured the giblets of a chicken cooked down with butter and gravy (or supply with an onion mixture if the gravy is lacking)
Cut the giblets after cooking to the size of a chickpea

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crocchette di Riso Semplici (Simple Rice Croquettes)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the rice very firm in milk, and at half cooking add the butter and salt it
Remove from the fire and pour in the parmesan
While still boiling, break in one egg stirring immediately to incorporate it
When well cooled, take it up in spoonfuls and roll it in breadcrumbs giving it a cylindrical form; with this amount you will get twelve croquettes
Beat the remaining egg, drop the croquettes into it one by one, roll them again in breadcrumbs and fry them
They can be served alone but better accompanied with other types of fried foods

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostate (Fruit Tarts)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: shortcrust pastry (full dose from recipe B No. 589, or half dose from recipe A)
lemon zest or orange flower water for flavoring

steps: Take the full dose of the pastry recipe B No. 589, or half of recipe A
Beat one whole egg and one yolk together separately; reserve some egg for glazing the surface of the tart
Add flavoring to the shortcrust pastry, such as lemon zest or orange flower water; recipe C is best
Roll out half the pastry with a smooth rolling pin to form a round disk about the thickness of a shield and place it in a buttered pan
Spread the fruit preserves or cream on top, keeping them separate if using both
If the preserves are too firm, soften them over heat with a few spoonfuls of water
Cut the remaining pastry with a ridged rolling pin into thin strips about one finger-width wide
Arrange these strips in a grid pattern over the preserves
Cover the ends of the strips with a ring of pastry made from the remaining dough, moistened with water to attach it well
Brush the surface of the shortcrust pastry with the reserved egg
Bake the tart in an oven or outdoor oven
It improves after one or two days

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di acciughe (Anchovy Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Wash the anchovies and remove their spine and small bones
Mince them with a crescent-shaped chopper, add butter in proportion, and crush the mixture with the blade of a dinner knife to reduce it to a homogeneous paste
Spread on bread slices like an ointment

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di beccaccia (Woodcock Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Woodcock innards, gizzards included but not emptied
Bread slices, elegant form, lightly toasted

steps: Clean the woodcocks and remove their innards, throwing away only the end of the intestine that borders the anus
Combine with these the gizzards without emptying them; some parsley leaves and the flesh of two anchovies for every three innards
No salt is needed
Mince everything very finely with a crescent-shaped chopper, then put it on the fire with a piece of butter and a pinch of pepper, moistening it with meat juice
Spread this mixture on elegant slices of bread, lightly toasted
Send these crostini to the table accompanied by the woodcocks that you will have cooked roasted with some small sage sprigs and wrapped with a thin slice of lard

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di capperi (Capers Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Bread slices, fried in good oil or lightly toasted

steps: Chop the capers coarsely
Clean the raisins of stems and wash them well
Cut the pine nuts into three parts lengthwise
Shape the prosciutto into very small dice and reduce the candied fruit into small pieces

Put a heaping teaspoon of flour and two teaspoons of sugar in a small saucepan over the fire; when this mixture has taken on a brown color, pour in half a glass of water mixed with a small amount of vinegar

When it has boiled until the lumps dissolve, throw all the ingredients into the saucepan at once and let them boil for ten minutes, tasting them meanwhile to feel if the sweet and strong flavor is right
When the mixture is still hot, spread it over thin slices of bread fried in good oil or simply lightly toasted
Serve these crostini cold, or in the middle of the meal to excite the appetite of your guests

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di caviale (Caviar Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Mix equal amounts of caviar and butter together
If the caviar is hard, work them a little on the fire with a spoon at moderate heat
Spread on bread slices like an ointment

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di caviale con olio (Caviar Crostini with Oil)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: If you wish to use oil instead of butter, add a few drops of lemon juice and mix all three ingredients well together
Spread on bread slices like an ointment

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di caviale, acciughe e burro (Caviar, Anchovy, and Butter Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a mixture of everything and work it to make it fine and smooth
Spread on bread slices like an ointment

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di fegatini di pollo (Chicken Liver Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: One shallot or one small white onion bulb

steps: Remove the bile sac from the chicken livers carefully without breaking it, doing this best while working in a bowl of water

Place the livers on the fire together with a mixture (battutino) composed of one shallot or, if unavailable, one small white onion bulb, a piece of prosciutto fat, several parsley leaves, celery and carrot, a little oil and butter, salt and pepper; but everything in small quantity so as not to make the mixture piquant or nauseating
At half cooking, remove the livers and dry them; with two or three pieces of softened dried mushrooms, mince them finely with a crescent-shaped chopper
Return them to the fire in the sauce that remained from the half-cooking and with a little broth finish cooking them
Before serving, bind them with a pinch of fine breadcrumbs and add a bit of lemon juice
The crostini should be tender, so make the mixture somewhat liquid, or dip the bread slices briefly, barely, in the broth

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di fegatini di pollo con la salvia (Chicken Liver Crostini with Sage)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Bread, stale crumb, slices about 1 centimeter thick

steps: Make a mixture (battutino) with very little onion and both fat and lean prosciutto
Put it on the fire with a piece of butter and when it is well browned, throw in the finely minced chicken livers together with sage leaves (4 or 5 for 3 livers should be enough)
Season with salt and pepper and, once they have released their moisture, add another piece of butter and bind them with a teaspoon of flour
Wet them with broth to cook them
Before removing from the fire, pour in 3 or 4 teaspoons of grated Parmesan and taste to see if the seasoning is right
Form the crostini from the crumb of stale bread, just under 1 centimeter thick, and spread them generously on one side only with the mixture when it is no longer boiling

After several hours, when you are about to serve them, either alone or as a side to roasted meat, beat an egg mixed with a drop of water and, taking the crostini one by one, let them touch the flour from the side of the mixture only, then immerse them in the egg and throw them into the pan on the mixture side

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di fegatini e acciughe (Chicken Liver and Anchovy Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the chicken livers in butter and when they have taken color, moisten them with broth; add a pinch of pepper, but no salt.

When cooked, mince them finely together with the washed and cleaned anchovy; then put the mixture back in the pan where the chicken livers were cooked, add a bit more butter, heat the mixture on the fire without letting it boil, and spread it on slices of fresh marrow bread.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di milza (Spleen Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the skin from the spleen and cook it with butter and meat juice. In the absence of this, use a small mixture of a little onion, oil, butter, salt, pepper and spices for seasoning.

Then mince these ingredients together with the anchovies very finely, put them back on the fire in the sauce that remains, adding a teaspoon of bread crumbs to bind them together, and without letting them boil further, spread them on slices of bread that you have first dried by the fire without roasting and brushed with butter.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di tartufi (Truffle Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Truffles, prepared as described in recipe 269

steps: Take bread sticks and cut them into diagonal slices, or prepare bread slices in an elegant form
Lightly toast them and brush them with butter while hot
Spread the truffles prepared according to recipe 269 over them
Drizzle with the sauce that remains

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini di Tre Colori (Three-Color Croutons)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: spinach, cooked with juice or butter and parmesan

steps: Cut the two chifels into thick slices one centimeter wide and fry them in butter or oil.
Take spinach cooked with juice or butter and parmesan, finely chopped, and cover the slices of chifel with a layer of the same.
Take two hard-boiled eggs, shell them, cut them in half crosswise and set aside the yolks.
From the white cut many concentric circles and place them over the layer of spinach.
From the yolk make many small pieces or small dice and place them in the middle of the circles of white.

In this way you will form croutons that can surround a roast dish which, having as a base fried bread covered by the green of the spinach, with the white and the yellow-red of the eggs will appear in three colors.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Crostini fioriti (Flowered Crostini)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cut slices of the finest marrow bread to the thickness of one centimeter, giving it the shape of almonds or small squares.
Spread them with fresh butter and lay two or three leaves of parsley on top, surrounding them with anchovy fillets in the form of little snakes.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Cuscussù (Couscous)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Vegetables of various kinds such as onion, savoy cabbage, celery, carrot, spinach, beet or other
Meat broth or tomato sauce or tomato conserve

steps: Put the semolina in a flat wide earthenware vessel or in a tinned copper pan, season it with a pinch of salt and a dash of pepper and, pouring over it drop by drop two fingers' worth (of a glass) scant of water, knead it with the palm of your hand to make it swell, become granular and loose.
When the water is finished, pour over it, little by little, a spoonful of oil and continue manipulating it in the same manner, lasting between the first and second operation more than half an hour.
Having conditioned the semolina in this way, put it in a soup bowl and cover it with a cloth, the excess of which, passing it underneath, you will tie tightly with twine.

Put the veal breast on the fire with three liters of water to make broth and after skimming the pot, cover its mouth with the bowl already prepared, so that the broth remains at some distance; but make sure that the mouths of the two vessels fit together and do not let smoke escape.
Leave the semolina thus for an hour and a quarter so it has time to cook by steam, open the wrapping halfway through cooking to mix it and then put it back as before.

Chop with a knife the 150 grams of lean meat, add to it a piece of bread marrow crumbled, season it with salt and pepper, make many small meatballs slightly larger than a hazelnut and fry them in oil.

Chop the vegetables somewhat and put first the onion to soften in oil and when it has taken color throw down the others, season them with salt and pepper, stir often and let them draw out the water they release.
Reduced almost to dryness, moisten them with meat juice, or with broth and tomato juice or conserve, to bring them to cooking together with the chicken liver cut into pieces and with the meatballs.

Remove the semolina from the wrapping, put it on the fire in a saucepan and without letting it boil dissolve into it the egg yolk, pour into it part of the said sauce, mix and pour it into a serving dish, but almost dry so it presents fullness, which you will decorate with the hard-boiled egg cut into small wedges.

Mix the rest of the sauce into the broth in the pot and send this broth to table divided into as many cups as there are diners, accompanied, of course, by the serving dish of semolina; thus each one draws down into his plate a portion of semolina and drinks after it the broth by spoonfuls.
The veal breast is served afterward as boiled meat.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce alla Napoletana (Neapolitan Sweet)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Le mandorle sbucciatele, asciugatele al sole o al fuoco e, scegliendone un terzo delle più grosse, dividete queste in due parti nei due lobi naturali; le altre tagliatele in filetti sottili
Montate le uova e lo zucchero in una bacinella di rame o di ottone, sul fuoco, alla temperatura di 20 gradi, battendole con la frusta più di un quarto d'ora

Ritirato il composto dal fuoco uniteci la farina mescolando leggermente e versatelo in uno stampo liscio, tondo od ovale, che avrete prima imburrato e spolverizzato con un cucchiaino di zucchero a velo ed uno di farina uniti insieme
Cuocetelo al forno a moderato calore
Dopo corto e ben diaccio tagliatelo all'ingiro a fette sottili un centimetro
Fate una crema: mettete al fuoco il burro con la farina per cuocerla senza farle prender colore; poi, resa tiepida, vi aggiungerete i rossi, il latte e lo zucchero rimettendola al fuoco
Con questa crema a bollore spalmate da una sola parte le fette del dolce e ricomponetelo, cioè collocatele insieme una sopra l'altra
Mettete a bollire in una piccola cazzaruola grammi 230 di zucchero in un decilitro di acqua fino al punto che, preso il liquido fra le dita, appiccichi un poco, ma senza filo
Quando comincia a diacciare spremetegli un quarto di limone e lavoratelo molto col mestolo per ridurlo bianco come la neve
Se v'indurisse fra mano versateci un poco d'acqua per ridurlo scorrevole come una crema alquanto densa
Buttateci dentro le mandorle a filetti, mescolate e intonacate il dolce, e colle altre divise in due parti rifioritelo al disopra infilandole ritte

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce alle Chiare d'Uovo (Egg White Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Whip the egg whites and pour into them the flour and sugar
Mix and then add the melted butter
When the mixture is fully combined, add the powders and lastly the raisins
Pour the mixture into a baking pan greased with butter and dusted with powdered sugar and flour, where the cake reaches at least two fingers high
Bake it in the oven or in a country oven and serve it cold

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce di Chiare d'Uovo (Egg White Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Whip the egg whites and pour into them the flour and sugar; mix and then add the melted butter.
When the mixture is all combined add the powders and lastly the raisins.
Pour the mixture into a buttering pan buttered and sprinkled with powdered sugar and flour, where the cake results at least two fingers high, bake it in an oven or country oven and serve it cooled.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce di Ciliege (Cherry Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Black cherries, raw, whole and stemless, 200 grams

steps: If you lack rye bread, use common bread.
Blanch the almonds, dry them and chop them finely to reduce them to about half the size of a grain of rice.
Work the egg yolks first with the sugar until they become foamy, add the breadcrumbs, the rosolio, the flavoring and continue to work the mixture a little more.
Add the well-beaten egg whites, mixing gently and pour it into a smooth mold that you have first well greased with cold butter and sprinkled throughout, and more at the bottom, with the said almonds.
Finally throw in the cherries, but to prevent them from sinking to the bottom due to their weight, mix among the mixture the remaining almonds.
Bake it in the oven or in a country oven and serve it hot or cold to four or five people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce di Cioccolata (Chocolate Sweet)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cut the sponge cake into thin slices
Grate the chocolate
Melt the butter in a bain-marie and in it pour the sugar and chocolate, working the mixture with a ladle until you have reduced it very fine
With this and the sponge cake dipped in rosolio fill in layers a mold that you will have first moistened with the same rosolio to be able to better unmold the sweet
In summer keep the mold in ice so that the mixture sets

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce di Mandorle (Almond Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Sugar, equal weight to the eggs
Sweet almonds with three bitter ones, 125 grams

steps: Blanch the almonds, dry them in the sun or by the fire and pound them very finely in a mortar with a third of the said sugar
Work with a wooden spoon the three egg yolks with the remaining sugar and the lemon zest until they become whitish
Add the potato flour, then the pounded almonds and the melted butter, working the mixture further
Lastly add the beaten egg whites and when everything is amalgamated together, bake it in the oven
Dust it with powdered sugar while still hot
Use a baking pan with a bottom diameter of approximately 22 centimeters for proper height
You can use the same butter to grease the pan, which, as you know, should be dusted with powdered sugar mixed with flour

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce di Marroni con Panna Montata (Sweet of Chestnuts with Whipped Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Healthy large chestnuts about thirty, 500 grams

steps: Cook the chestnuts in water as you would for roasted chestnuts, blanch them and pass them while hot
Reduce the chocolate to powder and then with all the ingredients form a paste

Take a large, round and presentable plate, place a small coffee cup inverted in the center and with a horsehair sieve on top pass all the mixture while rotating the plate so that it is distributed equally
Once the operation is complete, carefully remove and clean the coffee cup and the empty space left in the middle by filling it with 300 grams of whipped cream

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce Firenze (Florence Sweet)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Slice the bread into thin slices and toast them lightly
Butter the hot slices on both sides
Place the buttered bread slices in a concave and presentable dish that can be brought to the table
Scatter the raisins and grated lemon zest over the bread slices
Beat the eggs well in a pot with the sugar, then add the milk and pour this mixture into the dish over the ingredients without touching them
To cook it, place the dish over a low fire on the hearth, cover it with a countryside oven lid with fire on top, and serve it hot

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce Roma (Roman Sweet)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Apples of fine quality, not too ripe and medium-sized, 600 grams (5 or 6 apples)

steps: Choose fine apples that are not too ripe and of medium size, weighing about 600 grams.
Remove the cores with a tin tube and peel them.
Place them to cook with 2 deciliters of white alcoholic wine and 130 grams of sugar, taking care that they do not break while boiling, turning them, and that they do not overcook.
Remove them dried and place them with the hole vertical in a decent vessel that can be brought to the table and that withstands fire.
Prepare a cream with 4 deciliters of milk, 3 egg yolks, 70 grams of sugar, 20 grams of flour and vanilla sugar flavoring, then pour it over the apples.
Whip the three remaining egg whites, and when they are well stiff add 20 grams of powdered sugar and cover the cream with them.
Place the sweet in a country oven or only on the hearth with just its cover, with fire above and little below to brown the surface.
Before sending it to the table, brush it with the reduced syrup remaining from the cooking of the apples.
This will suffice for seven or eight people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce Tedesco (German Sweet)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Lavorate dapprima ed insieme per mezz'ora il burro, lo zucchero e i rossi d'uovo
Aggiungete la farina e il latte e lavorate ancora bene il composto
Mescolate nel composto insieme con le chiare montate il bicarbonato di soda e il cremor di tartaro
Versate il dolce in uno stampo liscio, imburrato soltanto
Cuocete in forno

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Dolce Torino (Turin Sweet)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cut the savoiardi in half lengthwise and soak them with rosolio, or better, half with rosolio and half with alkermes, so they can be alternated to make a better appearance.
First work the butter with the sugar and egg yolk.
Place the chocolate, grated or in pieces, on the fire with the milk, and when it is well dissolved pour it hot into the worked butter, add the flavoring and form thus a paste by mixing it well.
Arrange on the platter a first layer of the said savoiardi and spread them lightly with the said paste; then layer another layer of savoiardi, then a third layer still, always spreading them lightly.
Pour all the remaining paste over and at the sides, evening it out as well as you can.

The next day, before serving it, smooth it all over the surface with the blade of a knife heated by fire, and at the same time, if you like, decorate it with a sprinkling of pistachios or slightly toasted hazelnuts, both finely chopped.
40 grams of hazelnuts weighed with shell or 15 grams of pistachios will suffice.
This is a portion for six or seven people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Donzelline (Little Maidens)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a dough neither too stiff nor too soft, work it much by hand on a work surface and stretch it into a sheet the thickness of a coin. Cut it into small almond shapes, fry it in lard or oil, and you will see it puff, becoming tender and delicate to the taste.
Dust the donzelline with powdered sugar when they are no longer hot.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Donzelline Aromatiche (Aromatic Fried Pastry Diamonds)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: White wine or Marsala, two spoonfuls

steps: Chop the sage with a half-moon knife.
Mix the flour with all the ingredients, working it well and ensuring the dough remains rather soft.
Stretch it with a rolling pin to the thickness of a coin, dusting with flour if necessary, and cut into almond shapes.
Fry in oil or lard. This quantity is sufficient for four people.
Some people eat them together with figs and ham.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Donzelline Ripiene di Acciughe Salate (Fried Pastry Parcels Filled with Salted Anchovies)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Mix flour with butter, milk, and salt to form a dough of proper consistency, working it well if you want the pasta to puff in the pan.
Let it rest briefly, then cut it in half and stretch both pieces open somewhat.

Clean the anchovies, divide them lengthwise in half, remove the bone, and cut them into small square pieces. Place these spread over one of the pasta pieces, cover with the other piece to seal them together.
Stretch the united pieces with a rolling pin to a thin sheet and cut into almond shapes.
Fry in oil. This amount is sufficient for six people and can serve as a first course at breakfast or as an accompaniment to a fish fry.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Elisir di china (Elixir of Quinine)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Dried rind of bitter orange bruised, 5 grams

steps: First mix 250 grams of the said alcohol with 150 grams of the said water, and in this mixture place in infusion the quinine and orange rind, keeping it in a tepid place for about ten days, stirring the vessel at least once a day
Then strain it through cloth squeezing well so that all the substance comes out, and filter it through paper

After this, dissolve the sugar in the fire in the remaining 550 grams of water without letting it boil and pass it through a sieve, or better through cloth, to clean it of any impurity if there were any
Add the remaining 450 grams of alcohol, mix everything together and the elixir will be done
Before filtering it taste it and if it seems too strong to you add water

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fagiuoli a guisa d'uccellini (Beans Like Little Birds)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the beans first in water and drain them well
Put a pan on the heat with oil in proportion and several sage leaves
When the oil crackles strongly, throw in the beans and season with salt and pepper
Sauté them until they draw in the fat, shaking the pan from time to time to mix them
Pour a little simple tomato sauce over them
When the sauce has incorporated, remove from heat
These beans work very well as a side dish to boiled meat, if you don't want to eat them alone

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fagiuoli sgranati per contorno al lesso (Shelled Beans as a Side to Boiled Meat)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: a small bundle of 4 or 5 sage leaves

steps: Put the beans on the heat with all the above ingredients
Let them boil slowly and shake them often
Remove the sage and dried meat
Serve
This side dish is enough for four people

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fagiuolini colla balsamella (Green Beans with Béchamel Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: béchamel sauce made with cream, butter and flour
bread fried and cut into almond shapes

steps: Boil the green beans with soda so they remain a nice green color
Sauté them lightly in butter so they do not lose their color
Season with salt and pepper
Pour a flowing béchamel sauce over them, not too abundant, made with cream, butter and flour
Serve with a border of fried bread cut into almond shapes
They can be served as an intermediate course in a meal

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fagiuolini con l'odore di vaniglia (Green Beans with Vanilla Scent)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Soak the green beans in fresh water
If they are tender, put them whole and raw into a stew without draining them too much
Make a soffritto with oil, shallot, parsley, carrot and celery, all finely chopped
Season with salt and pepper, and when it takes color, dilute with broth or pass it through a strainer, squeezing well
To this strained sauce, add tomato sauce
Throw in the green beans to cook them
Before removing them from heat, season with two teaspoons of vanilla sugar
If this flavor is not pleasing, substitute with nepitella

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fagiuolini dall'occhio in erba all'aretina (Fresh-Shelled Eye Beans Aretina Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Trim both ends and cut into three parts
Put them in a pot with two whole cloves of garlic, raw tomato sauce, and enough cold water to cover
Season with oil, salt and pepper
Place over heat and boil slowly until completely cooked
Make sure some sauce remains concentrated to make them more pleasant
They can serve as an intermediate course or as a side dish to boiled meat

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fagiuolini e Zucchine alla Sautè (Green Beans and Zucchini Sautéed)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Salt and pepper, in small quantity

steps: If it is green beans, boil them halfway; if zucchini leave them raw cut into wedges or small pieces.
Put them to brown in butter when this, boiling, will have taken a hazelnut color.
For seasoning put only salt and pepper in small quantity.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fagiuolini e Zucchine alla Sautè with Sauce (Green Beans and Zucchini Sautéed with Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Meat gravy or tomato sauce from recipe 125

steps: If it is green beans, boil them halfway; if zucchini leave them raw cut into wedges or small pieces.
Put them to brown in butter when this, boiling, will have taken a hazelnut color.

After cooked in this manner you may add a little meat gravy or a little tomato sauce from recipe 125, which will no longer follow the rules of foreign or modern cuisine; but you will feel, in my opinion, a better taste and the stomach will be more satisfied.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fagiuolini in salsa d'uovo (Green Beans in Egg Sauce)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove both ends and the string from the green beans
Blanch them in salted water until half-cooked
Drain and cut into three pieces
Sauté with butter, salt and pepper to taste
Whisk together the egg yolk, flour, and lemon juice in a pot
Dilute the mixture with one ladle of degreased cold broth
Place over heat, stirring constantly with a spoon, until it becomes a flowing cream
Pour the sauce over the green beans
Keep them on the heat a little longer so the sauce incorporates well
Serve as a side dish to boiled meat

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Farinata Gialla di Magro (Yellow Cornmeal Polenta Lean Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Half a head of white or savoy cabbage, chopped
Two cloves of garlic, whole and peeled
Tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water

steps: Put the beans on the fire with proportioned water.

After they are cooked, pass them through a sieve and mix the paste in the broth of the same beans and in the same put to boil, for about two hours, the chopped cabbage which you will season with salt, pepper and thyme leaves.

Put a pan on the fire with oil in good measure and two whole peeled cloves of garlic; when these are well browned throw them away and add to the oil tomato juice or conserve dissolved in water and also here another little salt and pepper.
When it has boiled somewhat, pour also this seasoning into the pot where the broth and cabbage are.

Finally, when this is cooked, pour with one hand, little by little, the cornmeal flour; with the other hand mix well, so that lumps do not form, and when it has reached a certain consistency, that is somewhat liquid, let it boil a little more and serve it.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fave alla romana o dei morti (Roman Beans or Beans of the Dead) - First Recipe
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lemon peel flavoring, or cinnamon, or orange blossom water

steps: Blanch the almonds and pound them with the sugar to the size of about half a grain of rice.
Mix them with the flour together with the other ingredients and form a somewhat soft dough with as much rosoli or brandy as needed.
Shape into small pastries, in the form of a large bean, which will yield about 60 or 70 for each recipe.
Arrange them on a copper baking sheet first greased with lard or butter and dusted with flour; brush with egg.
Bake in the oven or country oven, noting that, being small, they cook quickly.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fave alla romana o dei morti (Roman Beans or Beans of the Dead) - Second Recipe
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lemon peel flavoring, or cinnamon, or orange blossom water

steps: Blanch the almonds and pound them with the sugar to the size of about half a grain of rice.
Mix them with the flour together with the other ingredients and form a somewhat soft dough with as much rosoli or brandy as needed.
Shape into small pastries, in the form of a large bean, which will yield about 60 or 70 for each recipe.
Arrange them on a copper baking sheet first greased with lard or butter and dusted with flour; brush with egg.
Bake in the oven or country oven, noting that, being small, they cook quickly.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fave Fresche in Stufa (Fresh Fava Beans Braised)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Take pods of large fava beans and shell and peel them.
Finely chop a young onion, put it on the fire with oil, and when it begins to brown, throw into the soffritto prosciutto cut into cubes.

After a short time add the fava beans, season with pepper and a little salt, and when they have taken on the seasoning, add one or two heads of lettuce cut into large pieces and finish cooking them with broth if needed.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fegatelli in Conserva (Pork Liver Pâtés in Preserves)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make pork liver pâtés seasoned with oil, pepper and salt, wrapped in netting and cooked on the grill, on a spit or in a pan.
After cooking, place them in a pot and fill it with rendered lard at boiling temperature.
Remove them as needed for use and reheat them.
Some use cooking the pâtés between two bay leaves, or as in Tuscany, add some fennel seed to the seasoning, but these are strong flavors that many stomachs cannot tolerate.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fegato alla Cacciatora (Hunter-Style Liver)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: good red wine, less than half a glass

steps: Slice three large onions and soak them in fresh water for one or two hours.
Drain the water and put the onion in a pan to dry it; once dry, add the lard to fry it.
When it has taken on a brown color, add the liver cut into thin slices.
Let it soften somewhat, mixed with the onion; then pour less than half a glass of good red wine into the pan.
After five minutes, stirring constantly, serve it seasoned with salt and pepper.
Note that this is not a dish for delicate stomachs.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fegato col Vino Bianco (Liver with White Wine)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cut the liver into thin slices and fry it in a pan with oil and butter as is.
Beat a tablespoon of flour with excellent dry white wine in a small pot to form a very liquid mixture.
When the liver is two-thirds cooked, pour this mixture over it.
Finish cooking and season with salt and pepper.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fegato d'Oca (Goose Liver)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: After cooking in the way indicated (in recipe 548), remove it dry and bind it with a mixture made of 20 grams of butter put on the fire with a heaping teaspoon of flour and, when this has taken a hazelnut color, dilute it with a ladle of broth and three tablespoons of Marsala wine, pour in the liver, let it boil again for a bit and serve it.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fegato di Maiale Fritto (Fried Pork Liver)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: To feel the true taste of pork liver you must fry it natural, in thin slices, in virgin lard and mixed with pancreas in small pieces
Remove it from the pan with a little of its fat, season with salt and pepper and while still boiling squeeze a lemon over it, whose acid serves to temper the greasiness
The thin slices of liver can also be floured before frying

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fegato di Vitella di Latte alla Militare (Milk-fed Calf Liver Military Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Mince a shallot or young onion finely and brown it in oil and butter
When it has taken on a deep red color, add the liver cut into thin slices
At mid-cooking, season with salt, pepper and a pinch of minced parsley
Let it boil gently so it remains juicy and serve it with its juice, adding the juice of a lemon when you serve it

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Filetti di Sogliole col Vino (Sole Fillets with Wine)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: sole fish, at least 150 grams each

steps: Take sole at least 150 grams each, remove the head and skin
With a sharp knife, separate the flesh from the bones to obtain four long fillets per sole, or eight if the sole are very large
Using the back of the knife, beat the fillets lightly and flatten them thin with the blade
Leave them in beaten egg seasoned with salt and pepper for several hours
Coat in breadcrumbs and fry in oil
Pour a little of the remaining oil from the pan and a piece of butter into a pan or dish where the fillets can lie flat
Arrange the fillets and season again lightly with salt and pepper
When they have browned a little, wet them with dry white wine, let boil for five minutes together with a little chopped parsley
Serve with the sauce, sprinkling with a pinch of parmesan
Serve with lemon wedges

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Filetto alla parigina (Fillet Parisian Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: round braciole from the best part of beef fillet, about half a finger thick

steps: Have the butcher cut for you round braciole from the best part of beef fillet, about half a finger thick.
Sauté them in butter after it has taken color over lively fire; salt and pepper for seasoning.
When they have formed a crust on all sides so that they remain juicy and slightly undercooked inside, sprinkle a pinch of chopped parsley over them and remove them immediately.

Before taking them to the table, cover them with meat gravy or similar sauce, or, which is simpler, into the juice remaining after cooking throw a pinch of flour and with broth make a mixture and use this instead of the sauce.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Filetto colla marsala (Fillet with Marsala Wine)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: fillet of beef, approximately one kilogram

steps: Tie the fillet and place it over the fire with a medium-sized onion sliced into thin strips, together with some slices of prosciutto and a piece of butter; season lightly with salt and pepper.
When it has been browned on all sides and the onion consumed, sprinkle a pinch of flour over it, let it take color and then moisten it with broth or water.

Cook slowly, then strain the sauce, degrease it and with this and three fingers (of a glass) of Marsala return it to the fire to boil again, but slowly; serve it with reduced sauce, but not too thick from too much flour.
You can also insert lard into the fillet and cook it with only butter and Marsala.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Finocchi colla balsamella (Fennel with Béchamel)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Take fleshy fennel, clean them from hard leaves, cut them into small pieces, wash them and blanch them in salted water.
Put them to fry in butter and, when they have absorbed it, finish cooking them entirely with milk.
Taste them to see if they are well salted, then remove them dry and place them on a tray that can withstand fire.
Dust them with Parmesan and cover them with béchamel.
Brown them with fire from above and serve them with boiled meat or stew.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Finocchi per contorno (Fennel as a Side Dish)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: After cutting them into pieces and blanching them in salted water, fry them in butter, finish cooking them with broth, bind them with a pinch of flour and when you remove them, season them with a little Parmesan.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Focaccia alla Portoghese (Portuguese-Style Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: First work the egg yolks with the sugar, add the flour, then the almonds peeled and pounded fine with a spoonful of the said sugar.
Add the juice passed from the oranges and the superficial skin scraped from only one orange.
Last unite to the mixture the whites beaten until stiff, pour it into a paper box greased with butter, about the thickness of a finger and a half and cook it in the oven at very moderate heat.
After it is cooked, cover it with a white crust as at No. 789.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Focaccia alla Tedesca (German-style Flatbread)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: candied fruit in small pieces, 30 grams

steps: Work first the egg yolks with the sugar until they have become almost white; add the breadcrumbs, then the candied fruit and raisins, and finally the well-beaten egg whites. Mix gently so as not to deflate them and when the mixture is all combined, pour it into a buttered and floured pan or dusted with breadcrumbs, where it rises about two fingers high and bake it in the oven; this cake will take on the appearance of sponge cake which you will dust, after baking, with powdered sugar.
If it is to serve ten or twelve people, double the amount.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Focaccia coi Siccioli (Flatbread with Cracklings)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Once you have formed the dough, working it little, add the cracklings chopped fine, grease a copper pan with lard and pour the dough in, pressing it with your knuckles so it comes out bumpy; but do not keep it higher than one finger.

Before passing it to the oven, make cuts if you want to serve it in pieces when cooked, square cuts with the point of a knife, repeating them halfway through cooking because they easily close, and when it is cooked dust it with powdered sugar.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Folaghe in Umido (Braised Coots)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 3 eggs of pappardelle or 500 grams strips

steps: After plucking the coots and singing them by flame to remove the down, gut them and wash them well.

Pierce them lengthwise through the body with a hot spit, then cut them into four parts throwing away the head, feet and wing tips; then keep them soaking in vinegar for an hour and afterward wash them several times in fresh water.
Do the same with the gizzards after emptying, washing and cutting them into four pieces.

Make a finely chopped mixture with a large onion and all the herbs in proportion, that is celery, carrot and parsley, and put it on the fire with 80 grams of butter, and at the same time the coots and gizzards seasoning them with salt, pepper and spice flavor.
