When they are dry bathe them with tomato sauce or paste dissolved in abundant water to cook them and so that much sauce remains.

Once cooked, strain the sauce and into it add a coot breast and a half finely chopped and another 40 grams of butter, to season with it and with Parmigiano cheese three eggs of pappardelle or 500 grams of strips which, for their particular taste, will be praised.
Serve the coots with some of their sauce afterward as a main dish that will not be despised.
This entire preparation should be enough for five or six persons.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fricandò (Braised Veal with Vegetables)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: A piece of milk-fed veal from the thigh, all in one piece
Fat and lean prosciutto for larding

steps: Lard the veal with prosciutto.
Tie the piece and salt it sparingly or not at all because oversalting is the worst defect in food.
Stud an onion with two cloves and make a bouquet with carrot cut into strips, celery and parsley.
Put everything in a pot with a piece of butter, brown the meat and cook it through with broth.
When cooked, discard the onion and bouquet, strain the sauce, remove the fat and reduce it separately until it becomes a jelly that you will add to the fricandò when you serve it at table.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fricassea (Veal Fricassee)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Flour, 5 grams or one scant tablespoon
Salt and white pepper to taste
Fresh mushrooms, 100 to 150 grams (if in season), or a pinch of dried mushrooms

steps: Cut the breast into pieces leaving all the bones.
Put a pot on the fire with half the butter and when it begins to melt, pour in the flour stirring until it takes on a hazel color.

Then begin to pour the water little by little and then the bouquet which you can compose of some strips of onion and carrot, threads of parsley, celery and basil, all tied together, excluding the leaves because these could fall apart and spoil the fricassee, one of whose merits is to have a beautiful straw color.
When the water boils throw in the meat and the rest of the butter and season with salt and white pepper, which is the finest pepper.
Cover the pot with a sheet of paper held firm by the lid and let it boil slowly.
At two-thirds cooking time remove the bouquet and, if it is mushroom season, you can make it more agreeable with 100 or 150 grams of these cut into thin slices; if not, a pinch of dried mushrooms.
When ready to serve, remove the pot from the fire and pour in little by little, stirring, the egg yolks whisked with lemon juice.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittata a sgonfiotto ossia montata (Soufflé Omelette)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Beat first for several minutes the yolks with the sugar
Then whip the whites until very stiff and unite them with the yolks together, mixing gently
Grease a tray that can withstand the fire with cold butter, pour the mixture into it so that it fills it and place it immediately in a hot country oven
After five minutes in the oven make some cuts with a knife and dust it with powdered sugar, then finish cooking it, which will require ten or twelve minutes altogether
Be careful that it does not burn on the surface and send it immediately to the table
To make it puff better, some add a little lemon juice to the mixture

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittata colla Pietra di Vitella di Latte (Omelette with Veal Kidney)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Take a veal kidney, open it lengthwise, and leave all its fat intact
Season it with oil, pepper, and salt; cook it on a grill and cut it into thin slices across the width
Beat eggs in proportion to the amount of kidney, season these also with salt and pepper, and mix in a pinch of chopped parsley and some Parmesan
Throw the kidney into the eggs, mix, and make an omelette cooked in butter, which when the bottom is set, fold in half so it remains tender

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittata di Cavolfiore (Cauliflower Omelette)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 300 grams of boiled cauliflower, without leaves and stem

steps: Chop the cauliflower finely and put it in a pan with butter and oil, seasoning with salt and pepper
Beat the eggs with Parmesan, salt them, and pour them over the cauliflower when it has drawn in the fat
Keep the omelette thin so you do not need to flip it; if the pan is small, make two instead

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittata di Cipolle (Onion Omelette)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Slice the onions into strips about half a finger wide
Place them in fresh water for at least an hour
Dry them well in a cloth before putting them in a pan with lard or oil
When they begin to take on color, salt them somewhat
Salt the eggs before pouring them over the onion, taking care the onion does not turn black from overcooking

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittata di Fagiolini in Erba (Green Bean Omelette)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Boil the green beans in salted water and cut them into two or three parts
Sauté them in a pan with butter and oil, seasoning with salt and pepper
Beat the eggs with a pinch of Parmesan and a pinch of salt
When the green beans appear somewhat shriveled, pour the eggs over them

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittata di Spinaci (Spinach Omelette)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove spinach from water, boil it, and while still dripping, immediately after removing from heat place it in fresh water
Squeeze it well and chop it coarsely
Throw it in a pan with a piece of butter and season with salt and pepper
Stir frequently and when it has drawn out its fat, pour the beaten and lightly salted eggs over it
Once browned on one side, flip it with a plate and return it to the pan with another small piece of butter
If desired, add a pinch of Parmesan to the eggs

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittata in Riccioli per Contorno (Curled Omelette Strips as Garnish)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Boil a bunch of spinach and pass it through a sieve
Beat two eggs, season with salt and pepper, and mix in the spinach in such quantity as to make them only green
Put a pan on the fire with just a drop of oil to grease it, and when very hot pour in a portion of the egg mixture, turning the pan in every direction so the omelette comes out thin as paper
When well set and dry, remove it, flipping if necessary, and repeat or triple the operation with the remaining eggs
Roll these two or three omelettes together, cut them into fine strips like noodles, and lightly fry them in butter
Season with Parmesan and use these strips as a garnish for fricandeau or similar dishes

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittata in Zoccoli (Folded Egg Omelette with Prosciutto)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: thin slices of prosciutto, both fatty and lean

steps: Cut the prosciutto slices into pieces about the size of a 10 centesimo coin
Place the prosciutto pieces in a pan with butter
When they have browned slightly, pour in the eggs, salted very little
When the omelette has begun to set, fold it in half so it takes on the name of fish of eggs more properly
Add more butter to finish cooking it

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittelle di riso I (Rice Fritters I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Pine nuts chopped to the size of rice grains, 15 grams
Eggs, three yolks and one white
Butter, the size of a walnut

steps: Prepare the beer yeast as for Krapfen No. 182, mixing it with 40 grams of the said flour.
Cook the rice in the milk so that it remains firm, but set aside some milk to add if needed; to prevent it from sticking, stir often and move the pot to the edge of the stove.

Once removed from the fire and lukewarm, pour in the already puffed yeast, the eggs, the remaining flour (the 60 grams left), the pine nuts, the rum, and a bit more milk if needed; after working it somewhat, add the raisins and place the pot near the fire so that the entire mixture rises at a very moderate heat.
When it has puffed up, drop it into the pan by spoonfuls to form fritters that will turn out large and light.
Dust them with powdered sugar when they have lost their first boil and serve them hot.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittelle di riso II (Rice Fritters II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Butter, the size of a walnut

steps: Cook the rice very thoroughly in the milk, giving it flavor and grace with butter, a little salt, a scant spoonful of sugar, and lemon zest flavoring.
Once cooled, add a spoonful of rum, three egg yolks, and 50 grams of flour.
Mix well and let the mixture rest for several hours.
When you are about to fry it, whip the whites as much as you can, add them while mixing slowly, and drop it into the pan by spoonfuls.
Dust them as usual with powdered sugar and serve them hot.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittelle di semolino (Semolina Fritters)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Butter, the size of a walnut

steps: Cook the semolina in the milk, salt it when it is cooked and, once cooled, add the eggs and rum.
Fry them in oil or lard and serve them at table dusted with powdered sugar.
This quantity should be enough for four or five people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frittelle di tondone (Tondone Fritters)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Mix the flour with the said water poured a little at a time and salt it.
Drop this mixture into a pan to cook it in white with butter, oil, or lard and when it is set on one side, turn it over with a plate on the other side, and there is your tondone.
Now pound it in the mortar with the said flavoring and soften it with the eggs: two at once, the other four one at a time with whipped whites, working the mixture a lot.
Fry it by spoonfuls to obtain fritters that, puffing greatly, take on the appearance of bombs.
Dust them with powdered sugar.
If you like, you can add 100 grams of Málaga raisins to the mixture, but in that case first soak them for twenty-four hours in fresh water and then remove the seeds.
Should be enough for six people, or for four if you make half the recipe.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto alla Garisenda (Fried Sandwich, Garisenda Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: slices of prosciutto, fat and lean

steps: Remove the crust from stale bread and cut it into almond shapes or squares of about four centimeters per side, all of equal size.
On each piece lay first a slice of prosciutto, then slices of truffle, and on top a slice of Gruyère cheese.
Cover the filling with matching pieces of bread, pressing them together to hold them in place. Cut all components thin so the fried pieces are not too large.
Lightly moisten with cold milk and once it is absorbed, dip each piece in beaten egg, then in breadcrumbs, repeating the egg and breadcrumb coating twice so the edges are also golden and sealed.
Fry in lard or oil and serve alone or mixed with other fried dishes.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto alla Romana I (Fried, Roman Style I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Put on the fire a small mixture of chopped onion and butter, and when it is well colored cook a piece of lean veal of milk-fed calf in it, seasoning with salt and pepper
When the meat is browned, wet it with Marsala wine to complete the cooking

Pound it in a mortar and to soften it somewhat use the cooking liquid left over, and if this is not enough add a drop of broth and lastly an egg yolk; but mind that the mixture must remain rather firm
Now take some wafers, that is, thin pastry sheets, and cut them into small squares similar to those used by pharmacists for small lint pads

Beat an egg and the remaining white; then take up a wafer with your fingers, dip it in the egg and place it over a layer of breadcrumbs; on the same place as much mixture as a small walnut, dip another wafer in the egg, make it touch the breadcrumbs on only one side, that which must remain on the outside, and with

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto alla romana II (Roman-style Fried Sweetbread)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: One small truffle or nutmeg flavoring

steps: Remove the skin from the chicken and cut it into very small dice, doing the same with the tongue and prosciutto; slice the truffle into thin strips.
Make a béchamel sauce with the milk, butter, and flour.
When the béchamel is cooked, pour in the aforementioned ingredients and let it cool well before using the wafers as in the preceding recipe.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto Composto alla Bolognese (Composed Fry, Bologna Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Lean veal of milk-fed calf, stewed
Small brain, boiled or cooked in gravy
Slice of fat and lean prosciutto

steps: Take a piece of lean veal of milk-fed calf that has been stewed, a small brain boiled or cooked in gravy, and a slice of fat and lean prosciutto
Mince everything with a crescent-shaped blade and then pound it fine in a mortar
After add an egg yolk or a whole egg, depending on the quantity, and a little béchamel sauce N. 137
Put the mixture on the fire and stirring always let the egg cook
Add last grated Parmesan, the flavor of nutmeg, very finely chopped truffles and pour it onto a plate
When it is completely cold make from it as many round balls the size of a small walnut and flour them
Then dip them in egg and after in finest breadcrumbs, repeating the operation twice and fry them

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto d'Agnello alla Bolognese (Fried Lamb, Bolognese Style)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: lamb loin or shoulder and neck
tomato juice or tomato paste dissolved in water or broth

steps: Cut the lamb into pieces and fry it as the offal in the previous recipe number.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto di Cardoni (Fried Cardoons)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: After removing the strings from the cardoons, boil them in salted water
Cut them into pieces and sauté them in butter, salting them a little more
Flour them, place them in batter N. 156 and fry them
They can serve as a side dish with a meat fry or a stew

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto di Chifels (Fried Chifels)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the points from the chifels and cut them into slices about one centimeter thick which you will place on a tray. Put the milk on the fire.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto di Finocchi (Fried Fennel)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cut fennel into wedges
Clean them of the tougher leaves and boil them in salted water
Before placing them in batter N. 156, dry them and flour them

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto di Mele (Fried Apples)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Large apples of good quality, not too ripe

steps: Take large apples of good quality, not too ripe
Remove the core with a metal tube made for this purpose, which leaves a hole in the middle
Peel them and cut them into thick slices just under one centimeter
Place them in batter N. 156 when you are about to fry them; if you like the flavor of anise, which goes well here, add a pinch
Dust them with powdered sugar and serve hot

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto di Pesche (Fried Peaches)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Peaches, burrone variety, not too ripe

steps: Cut the peaches into slices that are not too large
Like apples and fennel, wrap them in batter N. 156
Dust them with sugar after cooking
It is not necessary to peel them

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto di Ricotta (Fried Ricotta)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Use any quality of ricotta provided it has not become strong; ricotta from Rome and Maremma are excellent
Let the mixture rest for several hours before frying
With the stated amounts the mixture will be somewhat firm, which is good so the fried pastry takes the shape of bombs approximately the size of a walnut

To give these bombs a round shape as possible, take up the mixture with a spoon moistened with the hot liquid from the pan, shaping it with the tip of a table knife, also moistened in the same hot liquid
Dust them with powdered sugar and serve hot as a side dish with a meat fry
Note: there is little sugar in the mixture because it burns and the fried pastry would not then take on a nice golden color

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto di Semolino (Fried Semolina)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Semolina of fine grain, 70 to 80 grams
Butter, the size of a walnut

steps: Put the milk on the fire with butter and sugar and when it begins to boil pour in the semolina little by little, stirring continuously with a spoon
Salt it and beat an egg into it; mix and when the egg has incorporated remove the semolina from the fire and spread it on a buttered tray or on a floured work surface to the height of a finger
Cut it into almond shapes and dip first in beaten egg then in fine breadcrumbs and fry it
Dust it with icing sugar if you desire it sweeter, and serve it alone or, better yet, as a side dish to a meat fry

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Fritto negli Stecchini (Fried on Toothpicks)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the chicken livers in butter and season with salt and pepper.
After cooked cut them into 12 pieces and do the same with the Gruyère and the tongue.
Take 12 toothpicks and thread the aforementioned 36 pieces on them; first the tongue, in the middle the Gruyère and at the top the chicken liver at a certain distance from each other.
Then, using béchamel sauce, coat with the same the three pieces so that they remain well covered; then pass them in beaten egg, coat with breadcrumbs and fry them.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Frutta in Guazzo (Fruit Preserved in Syrup)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Strawberries, currants, and raspberries, 50 to 100 grams each sort
Sugar equal to half the weight of the fruit
Brandy or cognac enough to submerge the fruit

steps: Begin with the first fruits that appear in spring: strawberries, currants, and raspberries, placing 50 to 100 grams of each sort in a vase
Cover them with sugar equal to half their weight and enough brandy or cognac to submerge them
Continue with cherries, plums, apricots, and peaches, all pitted and, except for the cherries, sliced into thin strips, always adding sugar and brandy in proportion
You may also add gooseberries, grapes, and some pears, but then taste the liquid and add sugar or brandy according to your taste
Once the vase is formed, leave it to rest for several months before serving

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Funghi Fritti (Fried Mushrooms)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Choose mushrooms of medium size which are also of proper ripeness
Scrape the stem, clean them from earth and wash them whole without soaking them, as they would lose their pleasant aroma in the water
Then cut them into rather thick slices and flour them before throwing them into the pan
Oil is the best fat for this frying, and the seasoning consists exclusively of salt and pepper which you scatter over them when they are still boiling

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Funghi in Gratella (Grilled Mushrooms)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: The open ovoli are most suited to this preparation
After cleaning and washing them, dry them in the folds of a cloth and season with oil, salt and pepper
They serve very well as a side dish to steak or any roast

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Funghi in Gratella (Mushrooms on the Grill)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: After cleaning and washing the mushrooms, dry them between the folds of a cloth.
Season them with oil, salt and pepper.
Serve very well as a side dish to steak or any roast.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Funghi in Umido (Mushrooms in Stew)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Clean and wash the mushrooms and cut them into thinner slices than the fried ones
Put a pan on the fire with oil, a few cloves of whole garlic, slightly crushed, and a good pinch of nepitella leaves

When the oil begins to crackle, throw down the mushrooms without flouring them, season with salt and pepper and, halfway through cooking, wet them with simple tomato juice; be however sparing with the seasonings because mushrooms do not absorb them well

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Funghi Sott'Olio (Mushrooms in Oil)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Porcini mushrooms (morecci), the smallest ones possible
Water, if needed to dilute strong vinegar
Optional aromatics: garlic cloves, cloves, or bay leaf

steps: Choose the smallest porcini mushrooms you can find; if there are large ones the size of walnuts, cut them in half
Clean them well from dirt and wash them
Boil them for twenty-five minutes in white vinegar; if the vinegar is too strong, correct it with a little water
Remove from heat and dry them well in a cloth
Leave them in the air until the next day
Place them in a glass jar or glazed earthenware vessel, cover with oil, and add whichever aroma you prefer: garlic cloves, cloves, or bay leaf (which can be boiled in the vinegar)
Serve with boiled meats

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Funghi Trippati (Mushrooms Prepared Like Tripe)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: This preparation suits ovolo mushrooms well and they are called trippati perhaps because they are treated like tripe
After cleaning and washing the ovoli, cut them into thin slices
Cook them in butter and season with salt, pepper and grated parmesan cheese
If you add meat broth they will turn out even better

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gallina di Faraone (Guinea Fowl)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: A ball of butter mixed with salt

steps: Place a ball of butter mixed with salt inside the guinea fowl.
Lard the breast with strips of lard.
Wrap it in a sheet smeared with cold butter dusted with salt.
Roast it on a spit.
Remove the wrapping at two-thirds of the cooking time to finish cooking it and color it over the fire, brushing it with oil and salting it again.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Galline di Faraone Arrosto allo Spiede (Guinea Fowl Roasted on a Spit)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Place a ball of butter mixed with salt inside the guinea fowl
Lard the breast with strips of lard
Wrap in a sheet of cold butter spread and dusted with salt
Remove the sheet at two-thirds of cooking time to finish cooking and browning by the fire
Oil and salt again during the final cooking

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelatina (Aspic Jelly)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: One calf's foot or 150 grams of calf's foot
Feet of two or three chickens
Two chicken heads with their necks
A finger's width (of glass) of water

steps: Singe the chicken feet over fire and cut them into pieces
Put everything into a pot with two liters of cold water
Salt sufficiently and boil, skimming, slowly for seven or eight continuous hours so that the liquid reduces by half
Pour the broth into a basin and when it has set, remove the fat from the surface
If it does not congeal, return it to the fire to reduce further, or add two sheets of fish glue
To clarify and give it amber color, finely mince 70 grams of lean veal meat with a knife and then pound it in a mortar
Place it in a small pot with one egg and a finger's width of water, mix everything well and pour in the cold aspic jelly
Do not stop beating it with a whisk over the fire until it rises to a boil, then boil slowly for about twenty minutes, during which taste to check the salt and give it color

For the color, place two pinches of sugar and a drop of water in a non-tinned metal spoon, hold it over fire until the sugar becomes almost black, pouring it little by little into the boiling aspic jelly to achieve the correct color gradation
Take a towel, wet it in water, wring it well and pass the warm aspic jelly through it without squeezing, and pour it immediately into molds
In summer, if it does not set well, place the molds on ice
When you wish to unmold it, pass a cloth dipped in boiling water lightly around the molds

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelatina di Arancio in Gelo (Orange Gelatin in Ice)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Soak the isinglass and, changing the water once, leave it for one or two hours.
Boil the sugar in half of the aforementioned water for ten minutes and strain it through a cloth.
Squeeze the orange and lemon into this syrup, passing their juice through the same cloth.
Take the isinglass that has been soaked and bring it to a boil in the remaining two deciliters of water and pour this also into the said syrup.
Add to it the alkermes and rum, mix everything and when it begins to cool pour it into the mold held in ice in summer and in cold water in winter.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelatina di Cotogne (Quince Jelly)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: White fine sugar, equal weight to the water collected

steps: Take quinces with yellow skin, which are more mature than green ones.
Cut them into thick slices half a finger thick, excluding the core.
Put them on the heat covered with water.
Without ever touching them with a spoon, boil them covered until well cooked.
Pour them into a fine sieve over a bowl to collect all the water without squeezing.
Weigh the water and return it to the heat with an equal amount of fine white sugar.
Boil uncovered in a pan, skimming the foam, until condensed, which you will know by the small pearl that the sugar begins to form, or if a few drops poured on a plate do not run too much.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelatina di Fragole in Gelo (Strawberry Gelatin in Ice)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Very red and well-ripened strawberries, 300 grams

steps: Squeeze the strawberries in a cloth to extract all their juice.
Boil the sugar for ten minutes in two deciliters of the said water and unite this syrup with the juice of the strawberries; add the lemon and strain everything again through a fine cloth.

To the isinglass, after having soaked it as in the previous recipe, bring it to a boil in the remaining deciliter of water and pour it hot into the aforesaid mixture; add rum last, mix and pour the mixture into the mold to set it in ice.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelatina di Lampone in Gelo (Raspberry Gelatin Dessert)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Dissolve 20 grams of fish glue in the fire in three deciliters of water
Mix in the raspberry syrup, Marsala wine, and rum
Sugar is not necessary or only very little, as the syrup is very sweet
Proceed as with the preceding gelatins
If making with fresh raspberries instead of syrup, use the doses from the strawberry gelatin recipe and follow the same procedure

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelatina di Lampone in Gelo (Raspberry Gelatin in Ice)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Dissolve 20 grams of isinglass on the fire in three deciliters of water and mix into it the raspberry syrup, Marsala and rum.
Sugar is not necessary or, if at all, very little, as the syrup is very sweet.
Proceed as in the previous gelatins.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelatina di Marasche o di Visciole in Gelo (Gelatin of Morello or Sour Cherries in Ice)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Morello cherries or sour cherries, 400 grams

steps: Remove the stems from the cherries and break them apart with your hands, adding some crushed pits.

Leave them thus for a few hours and then strain their juice through a cloth, squeezing well; let it rest further and then strain it several more times, even through paper or cotton, so that it remains clear.
Boil the sugar for ten minutes in two deciliters of the said water with the cinnamon in it, strain this also through the cloth and mix it with the juice of the cherries.
Add the isinglass dissolved in the remaining deciliter of water and finally the rum, proceeding as for the previous gelatins.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelatina di Ribes (Currant Jelly)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: White fine sugar, 80 parts per 100 parts of juice

steps: Squeeze the juice from the currants through a cloth.
Put it on the heat without allowing it to ferment.
Add white fine sugar in the proportion of 80 parts sugar per 100 parts juice.
Boil, not too much, until it condenses into the form of a jelly.
Conserve in jars like preserves.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelatina di Ribes in Gelo (Currant Gelatin in Ice)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Proceed entirely as in the gelatin of morello cherries from the previous recipe.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Albicocche (Apricot Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Flavorful and ripe apricots, weighed with the pit, 300 grams

steps: Boil the sugar in the water for 10 minutes
When cold, add the apricot pulp passed through a sieve and the lemon juice
Pass the mixture again before putting it in the sorbet maker
This is an abundant quantity for four people

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Amaretti (Amaretti Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Pound the amaretti very finely in a mortar and then place them in a copper pot, adding the sugar, egg yolks, and flavoring
Mix and gradually pour in the milk
Put the copper pot on the fire to condense the mixture as you would for cream, then pour it into the sorbet maker to freeze it
You will have a delicious ice cream that can serve, with good measure, eight people. Half the quantity can serve four or even five people

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Aranci (Orange Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Squeeze the oranges and lemon and strain their juice.
Boil the sugar in the water for 10 minutes, pour it into the juice, pass the mixture through a sieve one more time and put it in the sorbetierre.
Serve it in goblet glasses filled to the brim, or all in one piece.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Banane (Banana Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Bananas, 4, which when shelled amount to 240 grams

steps: Pass the pulp of the bananas through a sieve, add to this the lemon juice, boil the sugar in the water for five minutes in an uncovered saucepan, mix everything together and pour the mixture into the sorbetierre, making no economy of ice and salt.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Ciliege Visciole (Sour Cherry Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Remove the pits from 150 grams of the said cherries without damaging them too much and place them on the fire with 50 grams of the said sugar and with a piece of whole cinnamon, which you will then discard.
When they are syruped, that is when they have lost their rawness and you see them shriveled, set them aside.
Crush with your hands the remaining 850 grams of cherries, pound a handful of their pits in a mortar and mix them back in.

Pass a few at a time through a cloth, squeezing hard, these crushed cherries, to extract their juice, and the scraps that remain put them on the fire to extract their juice with the aforementioned two deciliters of water, let them boil 4 or 5 minutes, then pass them through the same cloth and unite the extracted liquid with the previous one.

Put all this juice on the fire with two pinches of powdered cinnamon and when it is about to come to a boil pour in the remaining 200 grams of sugar, stir, let it boil for two minutes and pass it through a sieve.

Put the strained juice in the sorbetierre and when it is well frozen mix in the syruped cherries so that they are spread equally, serve the ice cream in small glasses and you will see that for its goodness it will be appreciated by all.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Cioccolata (Chocolate Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Grate the chocolate and place it on the fire with the sugar and four deciliters of the aforementioned milk in a saucepan where it will remain confined.
Let it boil for a few minutes, stirring it constantly so that it refines.
Remove it from the fire, add the rest of the milk and pour the mixture into the sorbetierre when it is cold.

If you want this ice cream more substantial, increase the sugar to 120 grams and add two egg yolks when you remove the chocolate from the fire and it is no longer boiling. Mix, and return it to the stove for a few minutes and then, as has been said, add the rest of the milk.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Crema (Cream Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Use the recipe for cream: make a cream with milk, sugar, egg yolks, and vanilla flavoring
You will hear it is a delicious ice cream, well churned and very firm, if you know how to work it properly
This quantity will serve ten people

Instead of vanilla flavoring you can give the cream the flavor of coriander, burnt coffee, or toasted almond. For coriander, see Portuguese-style Milk, N. 693; for coffee, boil several crushed coffee beans separately in the milk; for toasted almond, make a brittle like that of N. 617, somewhat more cooked, with 100 grams of almonds and 80 grams of sugar; pound it fine, boil it separately in a little milk, strain it and add it to the cream

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Fragole (Strawberry Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Boil the sugar in the water for 10 minutes in an uncovered copper pot
Pass the strawberries through a sieve along with the juice of the orange and lemon
Add the syrup after having strained it as well
Mix everything together and pour the mixture into the sorbet maker
This quantity will serve eight people

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Latte di Mandorle (Almond Milk Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Mandorle dolci con 4 o 5 amare (sweet almonds with 4 or 5 bitter), 150 grams
Odore di acqua di fior d'arancio o di coriandoli (flavoring of orange blossom water or coriander)

steps: Boil the sugar in the water for ten minutes with coriander inside, as in the Portuguese Milk recipe, if you use it for the flavoring
Shell the almonds, pound them very fine in the mortar diluting them with a few spoonfuls of the syrup obtained and mix them to the same
Then pass them through a fine cloth squeezing well to extract from the almonds all the substance possible, repeating the mortar operation more times if needed
Unite the cream to the squeezed liquid, freeze it in the ice cream maker and when it is well firm serve it in small glasses
This dose should be enough for nine or ten persons

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Limone (Lemon Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Preferably use garden lemons which have a more pleasant taste and greater fragrance than foreign ones, which often taste of reheating
Boil the sugar in the water with some pieces of lemon zest for 10 minutes in an uncovered copper pot
When this syrup is cold, squeeze the lemons into it one at a time, tasting the mixture to adjust the acidity
Strain it and pour it into the sorbet maker
This quantity will serve six people

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Marroni (Chestnut Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Put the chestnuts to boil in water as if making ballotte
When well cooked, clean them of both skins and pass the pulp through a strainer
Put this pulp on the fire with the milk and sugar and let it boil slowly in an uncovered pan for a quarter hour
Give the mixture the vanilla flavoring with the vanilla sugar and pour it into the ice cream maker
Serve it at table all in one piece; if it should serve nine or ten persons double the dose

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Pesche (Peach Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Ripe white peaches, including the pit, 400 grams
Three kernels taken from the pits of the peaches

steps: Crush these kernels with the sugar and put them to boil in the water for 10 minutes
Pass the peach pulp, squeeze the lemon into it and, mixing everything, pass it all through a fine sieve
This will serve six people

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Pistacchi (Pistachio Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Blanch the pistachios with hot water and pound them very fine with a spoonful of the said sugar, then put them in a saucepan with the egg yolks and the sugar, stirring everything well.
Add the milk and place the mixture on the fire stirring with a spoon, and when it is condensed like cream pour it cold into the sorbetierre. This dose will be enough for eight people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Ribes (Currant Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Crush the currants and cherries with your hands, add the lemon juice and pass everything through a sieve, pressing well.

Boil the sugar in the water for 10 minutes in an uncovered saucepan to obtain the syrup, and when it is cold mix it into the described mixture and pour it into the sorbetierre. It will be enough for seven or eight people, serving it in small glasses. The cherries, besides their special flavor, serve to give the ice cream a more beautiful color.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Torrone (Nougat Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Make a cream with the milk, the sugar and the egg yolks, giving it the flavor of vanilla, and pour it into the sorbetierre.
When it is frozen mix into it the aforementioned ingredients. Blanch the pistachios and almonds in hot water; divide those into three parts and mince these to the size of a vetch and toast them.
Cut the candied fruit into thin slices and the squash into small cubes, which being red will make a more beautiful appearance.
If the milk is good, by boiling it for half an hour with the sugar in it, you can do without the egg yolks, but the mixture will then be of less flavor.

The almonds in this and similar cases come out better toasted in the following manner. When peeled and minced, put them on the fire with a spoonful of the said sugar and a drop of water, stir them continuously and when they have taken color stop them with another drop of water; pour them then into a colander over the remaining sugar and use them.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gelato di Tutti i Frutti (Mixed Fruit Ice Cream)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Well-ripened apricots, weighed with the pit, 100 grams

steps: Boil the sugar in the water for ten minutes, then add the pulp of the said fruits passed through a sieve, then the candied citron cut into small pieces.
Instead of apricots you can use burrone peaches, and strawberries can be substituted for currants.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Germano in Umido II (Braised Mallard Duck II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 1 celery rib about a palm long

steps: Put the mallard duck in a pot with 30 grams of butter and let it brown.
Remove it and throw a tablespoon of flour into the remaining fat, stirring with a spoon until it takes on a brown color.

Remove from heat and not at a boil anymore, pour half a liter of water over that mixture and put the duck back in; season with salt and pepper and let it boil covered until completely cooked with a quarter of an orange peel in one piece, a celery rib about a palm long and a piece of carrot, both cut roughly.
Finally strain the sauce, break apart the duck at its joints, put it back in its sauce squeezing the juice of the orange over it to boil it a few more minutes and serve it.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Germano in Umido II (Braised Wild Duck II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one quarter of an orange peel, in one piece
one celery rib, one palm long
one piece of carrot, coarsely sliced

steps: Put the duck in the casserole with 30 grams of butter and let it take on color.
Remove it and throw into the remaining fat one spoonful of flour to have it take on, stirring with a wooden spoon, a brown color.

Removed from the fire and no longer boiling, pour onto that mixture half a litre of water and put the duck back in it; season it with salt and pepper and let it boil covered until completely cooked with one quarter of an orange peel in one piece, one celery rib one palm long and a piece of carrot, sliced coarsely.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Germano ossia Anatra Selvatica (Wild Duck)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: one wild duck (Anas boscas), about one kilogram
30 grams of prosciutto, fat and lean together
celery, parsley, carrot, one quarter of a large onion
black cabbage or whole lentils for accompaniment

steps: When you buy a wild duck in the market, open its beak to observe the tongue.
If you find it very dried out, you can say that the animal has been dead for a long time, and then smell it to make sure it does not stink.
Empty the duck, keeping the liver, heart and onion; remove its head and the skin of the neck, after having opened it to extract the vertebrae, fold it back over the animal's breast.
For a duck that weighs about one kilogram, finely chop 30 grams of prosciutto, fat and lean together, with all the aromatics, that is celery, parsley, carrot and a quarter of a large onion.
Put everything together with oil in a casserole and on top of the mixture place the duck, seasoning it with salt and pepper.
Let it take on color from all sides and then add water to cook it through.

Cook the accompaniment of black cabbage or whole lentils in water and make it over in the aforementioned sauce: taste it to add, if necessary, a small piece of butter, which will make it more agreeable and flavorful, and combine it with the duck when you send it to the table.
Cut the cabbage coarsely and season it as well with salt and pepper.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gialletti I (Little Yellow Cakes I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: With half the wheat flour and the beer yeast, make a dough moistened with tepid water and set it to rise
Meanwhile, knead with hot water the two flours mixed together with all the above ingredients, except the raisins
Add the risen dough to the mixture when it is ready, work it somewhat, and finally add the raisins
Divide it into fifteen or sixteen parts forming as many loaves in the shape of a spool, and with the back of a knife incise on the surface of each an almond-shaped lattice
Set them to rise in a warm place, then bake them in the oven or a country oven at moderate heat so they remain tender

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gialletti II (Little Yellow Cakes II)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Holding them to the thickness of half a finger, you will make about twenty of these; but you can also give them whatever shape you prefer and instead of 20, keeping them small, make 40
Bake them as the previous ones and to knead them follow the directions as if making short crust pastry

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Girello alla Brace (Garetto - Braised Beef Shank)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Place the meat in a pot with only salt and pepper seasoning, no water or other ingredients
Close the lid of the pot with several layers of paper held firm by the lid
Let it cook very slowly
The meat will release a copious amount of sauce which it will gradually reabsorb
When it has reabsorbed all the sauce, remove it from heat and serve
It is almost better served cold than hot

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gnocchi (Gnocchi)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Breast of chicken, boiled and finely minced, 40 grams

steps: Cook 200 grams of large floury potatoes in water, or better by steam, and pass them through a sieve.
To these add the boiled chicken breast minced very finely with a crescent cutter, 40 grams of grated parmigiano, two egg yolks, salt to taste and a hint of nutmeg.
Mix and pour the mixture onto a work surface over 30 or 40 grams of flour to bind it and be able to pull it into sticks as thick as the little finger.
Cut these into small pieces and throw them into boiling broth where a cooking of five or six minutes will be sufficient.
This dose may be enough for seven or eight people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gnocchi alla Romana (Roman-Style Gnocchi)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Mix flour with eggs and milk poured little by little into a saucepan.
Add Gruyère cheese in small pieces and place the mixture on the fire, stirring continuously.
When it is solidified by the cooking of the flour, salt it and add half the butter.
Let the mixture cool, then in the same manner as cornmeal gnocchi, cut it into small pieces in a tray that can withstand fire.
Season as you go with the remaining butter in small pieces and the grated Parmesan; but not on the surface, because Parmesan becomes bitter under heat.
Brown them under an iron lid or in a country oven and serve them hot.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gnocchi di Farina Gialla (Polenta Gnocchi)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Salt the water and, when it boils, pour the flour with your left hand little by little and with a ladle in your right hand, stir continuously.

It is necessary that this flour boils a lot, and when it is reduced in such a way as to hold well on the ladle, throw it with a table knife in pieces into a tray and season each layer with cheese, butter, tomato sauce or preserve dissolved in water.
Fill the tray and send it hot to the table.
If you prefer them more seasoned, you can treat them like polenta with sausages or like bolognese macaroni.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gnocchi di latte (Milk Gnocchi)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Mix everything in the same way you would for a cream and place it on the fire in a saucepan, constantly stirring with a spoon
When the mixture has become firm, keep it a few more minutes on the fire and then pour it into a baking dish or plate at a height of one and a half fingers and cut it into almond shapes when cooled

Arrange these pieces one on top of the other with symmetry on a copper or porcelain tray that can withstand the fire, interspersing them with some pieces of butter, and brown them somewhat in a country oven to serve them hot

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gnocchi di Patate (Potato Gnocchi)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the potatoes in water or, better, steamed and, while hot, peel them and pass them through a sieve.
Mix them with the flour and work the dough somewhat with your hands, stretching it into a thin cylinder so that it can be cut into pieces about three centimeters long.
Dust them lightly with flour and, taking them one at a time, hollow them out with your thumb on the reverse side of a grater.
Cook them in salted water for ten minutes, remove them dry and season them with cheese, butter and tomato sauce, if you like.
If you want them more delicate, cook them in milk and serve them without draining; if the milk is of good quality, apart from salt, no seasoning is necessary or at most a pinch of parmesan.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gnocchi di Semolino (Semolina Gnocchi)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Cook the semolina in milk.
When you are about to remove it from the fire, salt it and add half the butter and half the Parmesan.
When it is still very hot, add the eggs and mix.
Pour it onto a work surface or a tray, spread it to the thickness of a finger and a half, and let it cool to cut it into almond shapes.

Arrange the gnocchi one on top of the other in a nice display in a proportional tray, interspersing them with pieces of the remaining butter, and dusting them layer by layer, but not on the surface, with the remaining Parmesan.
Finally, brown them in a country oven and serve them hot, either alone or as an accompaniment to a plate of stewed meat or prepared in another manner.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Granelli Fritti (Fried Testicles)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Boil them in salted water, then make a superficial incision lengthwise to remove the outer membrane composed of the tunic and epididymis
Cut them into thin fillets, salt them a little more, flour them well, pass them through beaten egg and fry them

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Gâteau à la Noisette (Hazelnut Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Peel the hazelnuts with hot water as you would almonds, and dry both the hazelnuts and almonds well in the sun or by the fire. Then, after pounding them very finely, mix them with the rice flour using two tablespoons of the sugar.
Work the eggs well with the remaining sugar, then pour the almond and hazelnut mixture into it and stir very much with a whisk. Finally add the melted butter and work the mixture again.
Pour it into a smooth, rounded mold that is somewhat narrow so that it comes to a height of four or five fingers, and bake it in an oven at moderate heat. Serve it cold.
This amount will serve six or seven people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Insalata di Patate (Potato Salad)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Celery rib about one palm long

steps: Boil or steam 500 grams of potatoes
Peel while hot and slice thinly into a salad bowl
Finely chop capers, pickled peppers, gherkins, pickled onions, cleaned anchovies, celery rib and basil together and place in a bowl
Chop hard-boiled eggs finely, then crush with a knife blade and add to the chopped mixture
Season the mixture with good oil, little vinegar, salt and pepper
Mix well until it becomes almost liquid
Use this mixture to dress the potatoes
Add oregano if desired
This portion serves six or seven people and can be kept for several days

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Insalata Russa (Russian Salad)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: The lettuce, which can be of two or three varieties, such as romaine lettuce (lattugoni), radicchio, or lettuce, cut it into thin strips.
The beets, green beans, potatoes and carrots weigh them after boiling and cut them into small dice smaller than a chickpea and likewise the whites and one yolk of the two hard-boiled eggs.
Leave the capers whole and cut the gherkins to the same size as the capers.
The anchovies, cleaned and with the spine removed, cut them into small pieces, and having done all this mix everything together.
Now prepare a mayonnaise (see N. 126) with two raw yolks and the remaining hard-boiled yolk and 2 deciliters of finest oil.
When it is whipped, add the juice of a lemon, season it with salt and pepper and pour it into the said mixture stirring well so that it covers everything.

Dissolve on the fire three leaves of fish glue in two fingers of water height in a glass after having kept it soaked for a few hours and, once dissolved, pour an amount the size of a coin on the bottom of a smooth mold and mix the rest into the mixture which you will then pour into the said mold to put it on ice.

To unmold it easily, wet the mold with hot water and if you wish to give it a more beautiful and elegant appearance, when you have poured the thin layer of fish glue in the mold, before adding the mixture you can make an ornament of various colors on it with the vegetables, the whites and yolk of the hard-boiled eggs mentioned above.
This amount will serve eight or ten people.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Intonaco di Cioccolata (Chocolate Coating)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.
steps: Put the butter and chopped chocolate on the fire and when well melted add the powdered sugar and spread the mixture on the cake when it is no longer boiling

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Krapfen (Filled Pastries)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Egg yolk, minced filling with gravy and béchamel

steps: Mix the remaining ingredients with eggs, melted butter, sugar, and salt
If the dough is too soft, add enough flour so it can be rolled out to the thickness of half a finger
Cut discs using a tin circle of the designated size
Make 24 discs total
Using an egg or similar tool, press the point in the middle of each disc to make an indentation

On 12 of the discs, place a teaspoon of the filling made from minced liver, sweetbreads, prosciutto, salted tongue, flavored with truffles or mushrooms, all cut into small dice, combined with gravy and béchamel
Wet the edges of the discs with a finger dipped in water
Cover each filled disc with one of the remaining 12 empty discs
Press a tin circle of equal size on top to form an indentation all around
Let them rise with gentle heat, by the fire or in a stove
When well puffed, fry them in lard or oil until covered by the fat
Serve hot as a fried dish or intermediate course
For a sweet version, fill with firm cream or fruit preserve and dust with powdered sugar after cooking

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Krapfen I (German Yeast Pastries I)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Beer yeast, the size of a large walnut
Eggs, one whole and one yolk

steps: Take a handful of the said flour, place it on a work surface and, making a hole in the middle, mix in the beer yeast with lukewarm milk and form a loaf of proper firmness, on which you will make a cross-shaped cut to better know if it has risen.

Place this loaf in a small pan or pot in whose bottom there is a very thin layer of milk, cover it and leave it near the fire so that the loaf rises at a very moderate heat: you will see that twenty minutes will be enough.
Once risen, put it in the middle of the remaining flour and knead it with the eggs, the melted butter, the sugar, and the salt.
If this dough turns out too soft, add enough flour to reduce it so that it can be stretched with a rolling pin to the thickness of half a finger.
Thus you will have a sheet from which, with a tin circle, you will cut out many discs the size indicated.
Assuming you make 24, take an egg or another tool of similar shape and with the point of it press in the middle of each of the discs to imprint it with a hole.
In 12 of said discs place a spoonful of a fine mixture made with juice and béchamel sauce, composed of chicken livers, sweetbreads, prosciutto, salted tongue, truffle flavor or

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Krapfen II (Fried Pastry Balls)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: less than one deciliter milk or cream, so that the mixture is rather firm

steps: Put the yeast in a cup with a spoonful of the flour and, dissolving it with a little of the said warm milk, set it to rise near the fire.

Then in a bowl pour the butter, melted in winter in a water bath, and work it with a spoon, throwing in the egg yolks one at a time, then pour the rest of the flour, the yeast when it has doubled in size, the milk little by little, the salt and the sugar, working the mixture with a hand until it reaches the desired consistency.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Kugelhupf (Hungarian Yeast Cake)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: 200 grams Hungarian or very fine flour
one whole egg and two egg yolks

steps: Mix the yeast with warm milk and a handful of the said flour to form a rather firm small loaf; make a cross cut in it and place it in a small pan with a veil of milk underneath, covered and near the fire, making sure the fire does not heat it too much.
In winter, melt the butter in a water bath then work it somewhat with the whole egg, then pour in the sugar and then the flour, the egg yolks, the salt and the flavoring, mixing well.

Now add the yeast which in the meantime will have already swollen and with spoonfuls of warm milk, pour one at a time, work the mixture with a spoon in a bowl for more than half an hour reducing it to a somewhat liquid consistency, but not too much.

Finally pour in the raisins and put it in a smooth buttered mold dusted with powdered sugar mixed with flour, where the mixture does not reach half the pan which you will place well covered in a warm place or in a place of warm temperature to rise, which will take two or three hours.
When it is well risen to reach the mouth of the pan, put it in the oven at moderate heat, turn it out while warm, dust it with powdered sugar or if you like (this is optional) sprinkle it with rum.

provenance.author: Pellegrino Artusi
provenance.sourceTitle: La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene

recipes.name: Latte alla Portoghese (Portuguese Milk Pudding)
recipes.description: From La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene.

ingredients.name: Vanilla flavoring, or coriander seeds, or coffee flavoring, which are those that suit best

steps: If you prefer the last one, grind several grains of roasted coffee; if you like the flavor of coriander seeds, which is as pleasant as that of vanilla, pound a pinch of it and, both the one and the other, put them to boil in the milk which you will then strain.
If the milk is not of much substance, let it boil also for an hour and a quarter.
Never forget the veil of melted sugar at the bottom of the mold. Follow the same procedure as the previous recipe, omitting only the burnt sugar.
